All files are stored in the subdirectory EManager (will be) created by EManager, which is located in the tool types set up directory (<setupdir>) is stored.

The following files are generated by EManager:

EM.window - contains the window positions of all
program window,
EM.prefs - the presets from the Preferences-
windows,
EM.sources - the source text list and the current file
from the Sources window,
EM.setup - settings from the setup window,

and during program execution:

EM.temporary - contains program output texts; This file becomes
Program end deleted.

A double-click on the program icon is sufficient to to start. All necessary settings (if available) loaded.

All settings files should always be with absolute Path names are given!

Starting the editor

The editor will edit in the main window via the button started. A new (windowless) shell process started the source text file as a command line parameter. give. This means that the desired editor of this feature is ready- Must ask! How the editor and the Queltext file are selected is in “Attitudes” is described.

Source code compilation

With the compile button in the main window, the compiler started and compiled the source text. The program starts as real shell process with its own output window, in which the Compiler messages are displayed. The source text is as if Submit editor as shell parameters to the compiler. The settings for the compiler, its options and the source code in the setting window.

Start compiled program

Using the Start button in the main window, the program can be started. For this, a requester appears, which asks (if necessary). Shell parameters (intended for shell utilities). It shall consist of: the choice between a shell or a "workbench" start (see BugReport), or the cancellation of the action. The program file name is subtracted from the ending ".e" by the File name of the source text file is determined. How it is set, is described in settings.

Settings for source text, compiler and editor

In this window, the compiler, editor and source text files, and the compiler options. It is possible that: use settings, cancel the action or Backup settings in a preset file.

Preset settings

Various files and utilities are set here:

  • a) file to back up the settings from the settings window,
  • b file for securing the utilities,
  • c) file for backing up temporary data and
  • d) Text indicator program for the aid window.

Execute the flag asynchronously only applies to the text indicator and and for the implementation of the assistance programmes. Implementation of this flag the execution of the main program is not blocked.

Execution of utility programs, creation of directories, deletion

In the list, a program can be selected and a selected executed will become. It should be noted, however, that not the contents of the string gadget, rather, the content of the selected entry is taken into account. The means that an entry must first be added to the list, before it is available for further use. In addition, it may be various fixed shell parameters and some internal parameters are used. This list can be found in a file (see Preferences) store. Attention! The list is sorted by alphabetical order! In addition, files can be copied/renamed, deleted and registers are created.

Internal parameters for the support programmes

The parameters are given in curly brackets "{}" and each individual parameters are defined by a vertical line "|" from the other separately ({PARAMETER|PARAMETER|PARAMETER 3=<string>|...) }

Description of each parameter:

DISPLAY = the text indicator for displaying the program
Giving used. For this purpose, the temporary file is used
(See presets).
*** negated: SHELL, WB (1)
SHELL = The program expenses are immediately in a console-
windows.
*** negated: DISPLAY, WB
WB = Starts the program as a windowless shell process (see
BugReport.
*** negated: DISPLAY, SHELL
SRC = Uses the current source text file as shell parameter.
*** negated: WB, REQ, PAT
REQ = A file requester allows a file to be selected as a parameter.
*** negated: WB, SRC
PAT=<pattern> = In the Filerequester, only the files that
to "<pattern>" (e.g.: PAT=#?.guide).
*** negated: WB, SRC
DSX = Removes a file extension (from "program.e" becomes "program").
*** negated: WB
INPUT = In a string requester,
Asked.
*** negated: WB, SRC, REQ, PAT, DSX

(1) means that these options, if previously specified, are deleted will become. Those not listed are all allowed. The parameter block is read from left to right and some Delete previous parameters. Different parameters require others, Without which nothing would happen.

Examples:

1) The program "ShowModule" shows the contents of an E-module. This requires u.U. to create programs. So let's leave the content of a Display modules (requested via Filerequester) through a text indicator:

E:Bin/ShowModule {REQ|DISPLAY}.

2) The tool "GadToolsBox" is a well-known (and helpful) program. Man can with

WORK:GadToolsBox/GadToolsBox {WB}

start. The tool SrcGen, which is attached to the E-packet, generates from the ".gui"-file an e-source text. Included in the list is:

E:Bin/SrcGen {SHELL|REQ|PAT=#?.gui|DSX}.

"SrcGen" requires the file entry without suffix, hence the "DSX"!

1. Introduction:

1.1 Preface:

"...again the X-th, this time the ultimate program on Mandel-" Bread quantities & Co..., will certainly moan many. Admitted Fractalics is also such. Although countless good programs on available in the PD market, I still tried a program to In addition to the actual calculation of the so-called apple male, chens, also does a lot more (see: 1.3 features). In addition, it is written entirely in "E", a programming language crossing between C and Pascal (Many thanks to Wouter van Oortmerssen!!!). It shall: thus prove the performance of this dialect (best feature of my work) In my opinion, the internal language exceptions. Furthermore, I have tried to program completely system compliant - that nevertheless problems under 3.0 arise is known to me (pressure with Strei) fen, IFF format faulty, but since after browsing all available books and program listings in various programming spoke still no solution was ready, I gave up the search (Maybe someone can help?) My address is at the end of this text.

...Ahso: fractalics was developed on a standard Amiga500 (yes, it There are still people who work with it) with 1MB of memory and 2 drives. As a programming language I have Amiga-E V2.1b by Wouter van Oortmerssen used. There were from approx. 2700 lines of problems with memory that is not more was enough for compiling, which is why I use every major function had to test individually and temporarily remove others from the source code. Finally translated then on an Amiga1200 with 6MB memory (Thank you again to Frank Rogin).

1.2 System requirements:

Fractalics should run on ANY Amiga, no matter what chipset and which operating system version it is equipped with. An 8-bit screen depth is possible on AGA machines, but not directly supported (Reqtools pallet requester shows only up to 32) Colors, finer color gradations than 16 values per color portion are due to Use of SetRGB4 not possible - Kick3.0 Includes with SetRGB32 for "E" were not available. Nevertheless, with prepared pallets, the 256 different colors must be displayed.

1.3 Features:

  • Separation between calculated data and actual image enabled
  • rapid calculation of different views of the same set
  • 2 different view modes (can be extended as desired in the program)
  • unlimited number of open quantities \ both from the storage
  • unlimited number of views per quantity / construction limited
  • Loading and storing the calculated data (without the actual image)
  • Interruption and later calculation possible
  • Color rolls (without interrupt, but still saves valuable computing time)
  • Save the views as an IFF image (ByteRun1, unfortunately partly).
  • Erroneous - Where is the error???
  • Loading and storing any pallets as IFF
  • exemplary printing in the background with PrinterCheck before printing begins
  • (Mucus, lard...)
  • simultaneous printing of several views should be possible on Amigas
  • with several parallel interfaces (could not be tested)

2.INMEDICABLE VALUES

All immediate values in E give a 32-bit result; the The only difference between the values (A-G) is either their internal representation or the fact that they have a pointer instead return a value.

2A. Decimal [decimal] (1)

A decimal value is a sequence of characters "0" .. "9", which possibly a minus "-" sign precedes negative numbers to be specified.

Examples: 1, 100, -12, 1024

2B. Hexadecimal [hexadecimal] ($1)

A hexadecimal value consists of the characters "A" .. "F" (or "a" .. "f" with preceding "$" sign.

Examples: $FC, $DFF180, -$ABCD

2C. Binary [binary] (%1)

Binary numbers begin with a "%" sign and otherwise exist only from "1" and "0".

Examples: %111, %1010100001, -%10101

2D glide point [float] (1.0)

Gliding Point Numbers Differ from Normal Decimal Numbers only by the "." sign separating their two sections. One The two sections can be omitted, not both. Note that that glide point numbers represent another internal 32-bit (FFP) representation possession. Chapter 12 contains more information about glide point pay.

Examples: 3.14159, .1 (=0.1), 1. (=1.0)

2E. Sign [character] ("a")

The value of a sign (included in double "" quotation- sign) is its ASCII amount, e.g. "A" = 65. In E, immediate character values are a string with up to 4 characters, e.g. "FORM", where the first character "F" the MSB of the 32bit "M" is the LSB (least significant byte).

2F string ('bla')

Strings consist of a sequence of ascii characters included in '' are. The value of such a string is a pointer to its first Signs. Example: 'bla' produces a 32-bit pointer that shows a memory area in which the bytes "b", "l" and "a" are find. ALL strings in E end with a zero byte ("0"). Strings can be format characters that are initiated with a slash "\" are contained. Either to bring in signs from some are unrepresentable for a reason or for use in string- formatting functions such as WriteF(), TextF(), and StringF(), or kick2 VprintF().

\n a line feed (ascii 10)
\a or ''an apostrophe'' (The one that also includes strings)
Escape (ascii 27)
\t tab (ascii 9)
A backslash
0 is a zero byte. Rarely used as ALL strings end with 0
\b a wagon return (ascii 13)

Additionally, when used in formatting functions:

\d print a decimal number
\h print a hexadecimal number
Printing a string
\c Printing a character
\z Set the fill-up byte to '0' characters
format to the left side of the field
Format to the right side of the field

The following field identifiers can follow \d, \h and \s:

[x] Define the exact field size x
(x,y) Set minimum size x and maximum size y (strings only)

Example: Printing a hexadecimal number with 8 digits and zeros at the beginning:

Number: = $ff
WriteF('\z\h[8]\n',number)

results in $000000ff

A string can extend over several lines if the individual Parts are connected with a '+' sign and a <lf>.

'This extra long string' +
'Hooked up over two lines'

2G. Lists ([1,2,3]) and Type Lists

An immediate list is the counterpart of the LIST datatypes, just as 'string' is the counterpart to the STRING or ARRAY OF CHAR datatype. Example:

[3,2,1,4]

is an expression that as a value a pointer to an already initialized has a list. A list in its memory representation is compatible with ARRAY OF LONG, with some additional length information at a negative offset. You can use these immediate lists anywhere where a function a pointer to a field of 32bit values or a list expected. Examples:

['string',1.0.2.1]
[WA FLAGS,1,WA IDCMP,$200,WA WIDTH,120,WA HEIGHT,150,TAG DONE]

The sub-chapter on list functions provides further information on immediate type lists.

3. EXPRESSIONS

3A. Format [format]

An expression is a piece of source code composed of operators, functions, and brackets, and gives a value.

Expressions consist mainly of:

  • Immediate values, as described in chapter 2
  • Operators, as described in Chapter 4
  • Function calls, as described in chapter 3D
  • brackets (), as described in chapter 3B
  • Variables or variable expressions (see 3C)

Examples of expressions:

1
'Hello'
$ABCD+(2*6)+Abs(a)
(a<1) OR (b>=100)

3B. Priority calculation and summary

Amiga E has no priority bill or anything similar. The This means that expressions are evaluated from left to right. You can do that. by embedding (partial) expressions avoid:

1+2*3 /* =9 */ 1+(2*3) /* =7 */ 2*3+1 /* =7 */

3C. Expressions

There are different types of expression that are used for different purposes. can be used:

  • <var>, consisting of only one variable
  • <varexp>, consisting of a variable, possibly with unary operators,
  • Like ++ (increase) or [] (Field Operator). Further information is available
  • in chapters 4D and 4G. <varexp> makes variable expressions possible,
  • Just like Lvalues in C.
  • Note that these (unary) operators do not take precedence over others.
  • have operators.
  • <exp>. Includes <var> and <varexp> and any other expression.

3D. Function calls

A function call represents an interruption of the current source code in which a function is initiated. This can either be a self-written function (PROC), or a function that is transferred from the system to It will be made available. A function call consists of the function name, followed by zero to infinite many arguments in two brackets () are included and separated from commas ",". Note that the arguments of a function are again expressions. Chapter 6 says how to create your own functions, Chapter 9 and 10 show the installed functions. Examples:

my function(1,2)
Gadget(buffer,glist,2,0,40,80+offset,100,'Cancel')
Close(handle)

Why a new game in the MineSweeper style? I wanted a game, whose colors were freely definable and run on the workbench should. But what I have found in such games, me If I couldn't quite satisfy myself, I just made myself written. With the predefined colors and the general outfit I have tries to orient on the DOSen original, although the colors otherwise freely selectable. In addition, there are a number other features listed below:

  • variable size of minefields

To start MineClone, just click on the icon.

After launch, a window appears with a number of fields. Over these fields is distributed a certain number of bombs, which Identification is required.

If you are sure that in a certain field a bomb You can mark it with the right mouse button. (one) Flags appear then If you are not sure, just still Click once with the right MB. Then the flag becomes a Question mark, a kind of "I'm not sure yet" mark. Click again sets the field back to the original state back. So that you can also be sure that a certain field contains a bomb, it is necessary to use fields with the left Mouse button practically open. If you catch a field with of a bomb, the game went (or in other words: you lost!) Otherwise, a number appears in the field indicating how many fields directly adjacent to this field have a bomb.

MineClone also offers a menu, which is only accessible because The right mouse button is needed in the game if the Mouse cursor is located at a point in the window where a click of the The right mouse button does not matter.

0. Important Notice and Copyright

This workshop is based on my own experience with modules. In other words, there are certainly even more effective methods of program- mation with modules and everyone is asked to do something more as mere typing.

Requests for improvement, error messages, etc. are self-understood. gladly accepted.

And for weak guys and other chaots:

This TEXT is © 1994 by Jörg Wach.

The text as a whole or as part may be written without my Consent neither in other disk or CDROM series except for the EPD.

An imprint of the workshop in magazines or other media I need my written permission.

1. Introduction

This workshop is intended to promote the use of the new module concept under Amiga E from version EC3.0.

In addition to general information, a practicable the creation of their own modules, whose Optimization and its use in own programs demonstrated.

At the same time, some information about the return- of several information from PROCs as well as the Practical use of Amiga data structures.

The workshop modules and all programs addressed herein are Also present on the disk.

Well, what else can I say? Simple: let's go...

2. Modules, what?

With the delivered Amiga E-Packet you have a lot of so-called .m-Files, only what are they?

In these so-called modules, in the older version of the Amiga E compilers (EC2.1, EC2.1b) Information about libraries and data structures.

Definitions of the data structures of the Amiga system are for the Programming of routines that use system functions, eminent important. Without these structures, everyone is forced to work for systems. calls to define needed data structures and values themselves.

But that means a lot of effort and who can already Remember about 5000 data structures and structural values in your head?

The data are to be distinguished in library information, data- Structures and constants.

2.1 Modules for Library Information

An example of the module “mathffp.m” from the “Modules folder” (Note: all modules were equipped with the program "Showmodule") which of the programs delivered to the compiler belongs to:

ShowModule v1.7(c) 1992 $#%!
now showing: "mathffp.m"
NOTE: don't use this output in your code, use the module instead.

LIBRARY mathbase /* informal notation */
SpFix(D0)
SpFlt(D0)
SpCmp(D1,D0)
[..]

SpCeil(D0)
ENDLIBRARY

That looks pretty interesting, right?

For those who do not belong to the System programming is privy, actually very little. And that's what it's supposed to be.

The example should only make clear that in the modules for Library's information is available that is ALL known without modules should have been. And who would like all this, please nice, type, only to use the MathFFP routines?

And so we are already at the first effect of the modules: they Save time!

One and the same module can be used in different programs It is not and must not be entered anew each time.

How such a module is used in its own program, More later.

2.2 Data structures, constants

In addition to libraries, data structures play a major role in Amiga system. It can also be said that the data structures play THE role.

Constants describe values found in the data structures or in system calls may be used. Usually they are Constants nothing more than numerical values, but who already knows himself Does everyone notice? Therefore, each constant has been given a name by which this can be addressed.

And here we have again the same poblem: either all Typing information or .... well, you know, modules- turn.

Modules with data structures look as follows (example: gfx.m from) "Modules/graphics":

ShowModule v1.7(c) 1992 $#%!
now showing: "gfx.m"
NOTE: don't use this output in your code, use the module instead.

CONST BITSET=$8000,
BITCLR=0,
AGNUS=1,
DENISE = 1

(----) OBJECT bitmap
( 0) bytesperrow:INT
( 2) rows:INT
( 4) flags:CHAR
( 5) depth:CHAR
( 6) pad:INT
( 8) planes:substructure
(---) ENDOBJECT /* SIZEOF=40 */

[..]

On the one hand, we see a key word from E: CONST at the beginning. I.e. nothing other than that all subsequent entries constants are.

On the other hand, we see a data structure that also corresponds to the known E-key word "OBJECT" is introduced.

And what can we conclude from all this? We all have these Data helps to save time. A hell of a lot of time for Type in ...

2.3 Modules under EC3.0

With the older EC versions it was quite cumbersome to own Define modules. There was no function in the compiler and so you had to if you needed your own data structures as modules production were to be carried out through support programmes.

In addition, it was also not possible with the old versions, own Programs, PROCS or data definition as modules.

But that has now changed...

Since the version EC3.0 and following, not only Library information, data structures and constants but also procs, own data definitions, etc.

And that's the point. For this we will now enter into the Full boarding ...

3.0 Our first, own module - What should it be able to do?

Let’s start by outlining what our workshop module Let's do it.

Among the E-system functions is a name "KickVersion". These functions do nothing other than that based on the above- This version number checks whether the corresponding Kickstart Version is available or not.

If this exists, TRUE is returned, otherwise false.

The problem with this function, however, is that the actual Kickstart version is returned. And this can be problematic. be ...

For example, you want to write a program that both for Kick 1.3, Kick 2.04 and Kick3.0 have different routines. In this case: In case you have to call this function MORE times to check, Which version actually exists?

How about a function that makes this possible? Light?

In addition, I miss a function that also contains information about displays the CPU or FPU used.

Well, so there we have our functions of the WorkShop module together:

  • a) information about the CPU used,
  • b information about the FPU used,
  • c) Information about the Kickstart version used.

As a minor peculiarity, it should not have 3 different functions give, but only a single function, the three return values returns.

And to give the whole thing another name, let's call the module "SystemInfo"

As I said, this is a workshop on how to use modules. Surely you could also use other modules for div. Problems arising from throw, but that's what you should be able to do after this...

3.1 What do we need?

Well, let's start with point a.

Where do we get the information about the CPU used?

In the Exec library there is a constant that is ATTNFlag called. And right here it says what is used for a CPU in the Amiga will. Since this is a flag, the for- mations in BIT's, i.e. we have to check whether the the corresponding bit for the corresponding CPU is ON or OFF.

The individual flags in detail:

AFF 68040 ---> Amiga has 68040 CPU.
AFF 68030 ---> Amiga has 68030 CPU.
AFF 68020 ---> Amiga has 68020 CPU.
AFF 68010 ---> Amiga has 68010 CPU.

If none of these flags are set, then it is a 60000 CPU.

In addition, however, one can also recognize from the ATTNFlag, which FPU is available:

AFF 68881 ---> Amiga has 68881 FPU.
AFF 68882 ---> Amiga has 68882 FPU.
AFF FPU40 ---> Amiga has 68040 internal FPU.

If none of these flags is set, then no FPU is present.

We would have already done point b. How do we get information about the kick- Start version?

For this, one must know that every library in the Amiga system has a so-called "English Library". has version number. Not exactly with this version number from the Exec library can be found out which kick version of the Amiga used.

3.2 Let's go...

With the tools from the aforementioned chapter we can now ran and write a PROC for this problem:

/***************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************
Module. Syseminfo
Description. A module that determines and controls the CPU/FPU types
The kick version.
: Author. Jörg Wach (=JCL POWER)
:EC version. EC3.0e
:OS > 1.2
:PRG version. 1.0 -> Because it had to be
Without a Kick version
1.1 -> With Kickversion
************************************************************************************ /

OPT MODULS
OPT EXPORT

MODULE 'exec/execbase'
MODULE 'exec/libraries'

PROC systeminfo()

DEF execBase : PTR TO execbase, attnFlag, cpu, fpu, kick
libbase : PTR TO lib

execBase := execbase
attnFlag := execBase.attnflags

What CPU do we have here? *//

IF (attnFlag AND AFF 68040)
cpu : = 68040
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68030)
cpu : = 68030
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68020)
cpu : = 68020
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68010)
cpu : = 68010
ELSE
cpu : = 68000
ENDIF

/* And is an FPU on board? *//

IF (attnFlag AND AFF 68881)
fpu : = 68881
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68882)
fpu = 68882
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF FPU40)
fpu = 68040
ELSE
fpu : = 0
ENDIF

/* And kick version? *//

libbase := execBase.lib
kick := libbase.version

ENDPROC kick, cpu, fpu

Let's take the source code apart, where I block or block. The following lines are used:

1 The Commentary

As a programmer, you should never read the documentation that Forget the version number of a program, etc. That's why I've defined a standard block for myself. which contains some brief information about the source code.

OPT MODULE

This is a new keyword under EC 3.0 and says nothing else than the now following source code a module is. So the compiler also knows that it is from the source code not an executable program.

This keyword must UNCONDITIONALLY first of all for own modules stand.

OPT EXPORT

This is a special keyword for modules only. It shall be WHAT is known from the module other programs may be given.

In other words, this can be controlled by WHICH PROC's, Definitions etc. another program than from this You can know the module.

If this keyword is not used anywhere in the source text, then It means that all functions, constants, etc. are PRIVAT, Other programs may not be announced.

If this keyword is called second in the source code then all subsequent information will be pro- grams made known.

If only individual functions are known to other programs If it wants to do so, then it must do so before the respective functions. Keyword EXPORT is written.

Example:

PROC eins()

ENDPROC

EXPORT PROC two()

[..]

ENDPROC

This means nothing other than that the procedure one() other programs are not announced while the Procedure two other programs is made very well known.

You will certainly ask yourself: what is the point?

This is very easy to answer: if you have a main procedure have which invokes many underprocedures, with other programs communicate only through the main procedure, then it is un- sense, other programs the underprocedures also still known To do it, right?

The PROC to ENDPROC

Needless to say, since we know everything, I have clarified this in the previous chapters.

ENDPROC kick, cpu, fpu

As I said in the definition of objectives, all Values are output from this procedure.

And for this we resort to the special feature of EC3.0: the Return of multiple values.

Well, and so easily you can return several values ....

Yes, and that was all for the source code.

4. Generate a module with EC

I do not need to say much about this, as it is done quite normally. The only exception is that after the lines

Amiga E compiler/assembler/linker v3.0e registered (c) 91/92/93/94 $#%!
lexical analysis ...
Parsing and compiling ...
No errors ...

no "SystemInfo" file is generated, but a file with the name "SystemInfo.m", because we created a module.

5. Test of the module

Now that we have a module, we want it in See action.

For this we create a small test program that the module and the the PROC systeminfo() contained therein. The issue should be, quite banal, in the CLI.

And here's the test program:

MODULE '*SystemInfo'


PROC main()
DEF t1, t2, t3
t1,t2,t3 := systeminfo()
WriteF('\d \d \d',t1, t2, t3)

ENDPROC

There is only one particular reference to the test program: the first line.

It says "MODULE '*Systeminfo", which tells our program that it should use a module with the name "SystemInfo" and the this module is in the current directory.

How EC knows that this module is in the current directory Located? By nothing other than the "*" before the module name.

If the star is omitted, EC searches for the module in the ... drawing "MODULES:", where

Usage

10mins [-t] <text file> [-v60] [-s <seconds>] [-o <Output>] [-nb]

Parameters:

-t <text file> indicates the text to be displayed

-v60 selects a vertical blank frequency of 60 Hz
(default: 50 Hz)

-s <seconds> indicates the timeout after which the window is closed
shall be:
(Default: 600 seconds)

-o <Output> indicates the output
(Default: "RAW:0/203/640/53/Reminder/NOSIZE")

-nb turns off the DisplayBeep()
(Default: on)

Purpose:

This program opens a RAW: window, shows the desired text and waits for a timeout or <Ctrl c>. Then the RAW: window closed and the program ends.

Motivation:

I actually wrote this program for my own purposes. Use with CyberCron. CyberCron is a very good program with which can perform various things at specified times. I use the program to automatically netcalls on different mailboxes Do it at night (for example). If I am at this time If you are online, the netcalls cannot be performed. So I wrote this program. It opens its window 15 minutes before the Netcall (must be set in CyberCron). When I go to the computer If I sit, I can close the window again by <Ctrl c>. If not, closes itself after 10 minutes (must be set in source code) shall be:

My text files contain something similar to this:

ATTENTION: Netcall at <Mailbox> at <Time> clock !! Another 15 minutes!
Please stop all modem activities as soon as possible!!

Here is another example of using 10mins:

If a user wants to register in a mailbox, he usually has to Date of birth. Sysop can now configure CyberCron to 10mins calling a text like "A birthday congratulations mail" Send Blizzer!! It might as well be your birthday!

Kindly, Daniel sent me the source his information (since I am not so knowledgeable with Pascal, could I do not start much with the supplied "clouds" source: an arti- kel and an ABasic listing in Amiga magazine 10/87 - "Mathematical Clouds". I didn't look that far either, especially since the text of my opinion It was too superficial. So I just started the attempt. and "EClouds" (of course in E). And lo and behold, the whole thing resembled but very much my model programs (especially "plasma"); See End of Arti- kels.

@NS
@ZS2

[4m] How does the calculation work? [0m]

@ZS1

Take any number of color registers that have a color gradient. (e.g. from white to blue). In "EClouds" the colors 4 to 31. Now you have to decide on the size of the graph. Suitable are those who- te, whose logarithm to base 2 is even, so [3m32, 64, 128, 256, 512] so on. This value we call [3moriginal width, [0m even if it equals] tig describes the height. [3mOriginX [0mund] [3mOriginY [0m] describe the left, upper Corner of the graph.

At the beginning of the calculation, we need the colors of the four vertices of gravity. phik, wherein colors are limited in the following to the history registers:

[3m]
Point( OriginX, OriginY) = random color
Point( OriginX+OriginWide, OriginY) = Random Color
Point(OriginX, OriginY+OriginWide) = Random Color
Point(OriginX+OriginWide, OriginY+OriginWide) = random color [0m]
@NS

As you can see, the graphics are not 128x128 pixels in size, but 129x129. The has a simple reason: we are now invoking a routine that recursively calls itself 4 times. for each quarter of the rectangle of the last iteration, that is, you first divide the 129x129 rectangle into four small rectangles of the size 65x65, the edges of which overlap (at the Axis [3mOriginX+64,OriginY - OriginX+64,OriginY+128] [3mOriginX,OriginY+64 - OriginX+128,OriginY+64]. [0m]Before the routine itself 4 times with the respective rectangle of size [3mwidth/2] [0mauft, it sets the current key points, if they do not yet exist. In the first through- So the routine only calls itself 4 times without any corner points. This is because they exist (we have chosen random colors). Let's keep track of the whole thing: let's take the rectangle [3moriginX,originY,originwidth/2] Width [0mist in the iteration thus [3m64]. [0m] The routine now sets the vertices of the rectangle, with the point on the top left has already been set in the last iteration (or before the beginning of the inter- tions. There are still points on the top right, on the bottom right and on the left un- ten:

@NS
[3m point( X+width, Y ) = point( X, Y )
+ point( X+OldWide,Y)
divided by 2, plus random variation
(Old width = width * 2, in this case 128)
Point( X, Y+width) = Point( X, Y)
+ Point( X, Y+OldWide)
divided by 2, plus random variation
Point( X+Wide, Y+Wide) = Point( X+Wide, Y)
+ point( X, Y+ width )
divided by 2, plus random variation
[0m]

And you can get the clouds calculated. The calculation of the corners - always follows the above scheme, with points that are already set, na- Do not be recalculated! The maximum fluctuation value takes Usually, the smaller the rectangles get. With "EClouds" you can add a few values to the rum in the case of a shell start. Change the game:

[0m for a maximum variation of 4 color registers] [3mdefault = 2048]
BInit [0mBalance range for first iteration in [3mColors * 256]. [0mThis value]
is subtracted from the calculated random variation. If so,
[3mSInit/2 [0mist, find the fluctuation in white and in blue]
In fact, it's a little bit more than a little bit more than a little bit.
rather than white; [3mdefault = 1024]
SModify [0m is added to the last fluctuation maximum at each iteration, and
should therefore be negative (explanation see above); [3m default = -96]
BModfiy [0m is added to the last balance value at each iteration and should be
It is also negative. The ratio of [3mSInit [0m] to [3mBInit [0ment-speaks]

[0m]

Timm Baumeister (timm@…) wrote: : Hello! Can someone tell me how to get into E? Does something like string arrays work? Greetings Timm Baumeister - timm@…

Many a family tree needs trimming.

ARRAY OF LONG

because strings are nothing other than pointers on text But note that you have to copy the strings somewhere else. e.g.

StrCopy(text,'balfasel')
feld[0]: = text
StrCopy(text,'balblub')
feld[1]:=text

is not possible, because in text then every time something else is written and feld[0]=feld[1]=text.

What do you want to do specifically, then I recommend you an optimal method. If you just want to try it this way, you

for x = 0 to 9
text:=String(StrLen(<text>))
StrCopy(text,<text>)
feld[x]:=text
endfor

But if you think about it, that's a lot of waste of computing time and memory hacking (fragmentation).

Danny

timm@… (Timm Baumeister) wrote on 18.05.1996:

Can someone tell me how to get into E > something like string arrays?

Quite simply with

DEF a[20]:ARRAY OF CHAR

or

DEF a[20]:STRING

And if by "String Array" you mean an array with strings, then For example, it goes like this:

DEF a[20]:ARRAY OF LONG,i

FOR i = 0 TO 19
a[i]:=String(length)
ENDFOR

Or so:

DEF a:PTR TO LONG

a:=['String1', 'String2', 'String3']

(Just to show you some possibilities...)

Subject: String Arrays in E

> Hello!

Hello.

Can someone tell me how to get into E > something like string arrays?

DEF sa[100]: ARRAY OF LONG

This allows you to save the hands on 100 strings.

sa[5]:="This is a test string"

assigns the pointer to the string to the array at position 5 . So you can prove everything.

But beware of the difference String <-> E-String. Don't forget what is what!

For E-Strings, this would have to look like this:

DEF sa[100]:ARRAY OF LONG,s:PTR TO CHAR

s:='Test string' -> s is assigned to a normal string
sa[5]:=String(20) -> Get storage
IF sa[5]=NIL THEN Raise("MEM") -> the query
StrCopy(sa[5],s) -> Copy String

The filling of all elements with pointers on E-strings should be probably put in a subroutine. Then you just need more with StrCopy() to access the elements.

Goodbye! Jens "PGP-Key on Request"

ACHTUNG: Das Testprogramm "UseIFFImageClass" funktioniert nur korrekt,

source package on Aminet ↗

ATTENTION: The test program "UseIFFImageClass" only works correctly, If the file "ProjectBrushes" in the "Ram:" or "Ram Disk:" is located.

IFFImageClass:

This class is a subsidiary class of the ImageClass and allows the Programmer prefabricated brushes (brushes at DPaint, PPaint etc.) transformed into images. These images are made with the help of "EMakeBrushCAT" program in a so-called Catenation. This categorization then only has to be loaded in order to gaining access. "EMakeBrushCAT" is the e-version of "MakeBrushCAT" by Holger Engels. The biggest difference is the smaller Memory consumption and additional functions (instead of 57 KB only) 14 KB + ASL requester.

Use of EMakeBrushCAT:

The ListView counter contains the list of all brushes that are in of a catalog. The path of this CATENATION is entered in the text input field "Dest:". Man can enter the paths of the Bushes by hand or by means of Multiple dial in the ASL requester.

(Description is very short, but the program is really) Easy to use.

Using the IFFImageClass:

Types: iclass : PTR TO iclass <intuition/classes>
ifflist : PTR TO lh <exec/lists>
Tag: PTR TO CHAR
image: PTR TO image <intuition/intuition>

Step description

iclass := iff InitIFFIMAGEClass()
->: the private class is initialized
2. ifflist := iff InitIFFIMAGEList(path)
->: load the images of the CATENATION file
image := NewObjectA(iclass,NIL),
[IFFIM IFFLIST, ifflist]
ISD NORMAL, 'Normal',
ISD SELECTED, 'Selected',
NIL]
->: This command creates an image object
iff FreeIFFList(ifflist)
->: Release of the CATENATION again
DisposeObject(image)
->: Resolve image object
iff FreeIFFIMAGEClass(iclass)
->: dissolve private class

2 Direct Values

All immediate values in E give a 32-bit result; the The only difference between the values (A-G) is either their internal representation or the fact that they have a pointer instead return a value.

  • A. Decimal (1)
  • B. Hexadecimal ($1)
  • C. Binary (%1)
  • D. Gliding point (1.0)
  • E. Sign ('a')
  • F. Character strings ('bla')
  • G. Lists ([1,2,3]) and type lists

Previous Chapter Next Chapter

2A. Decimal (1)

A decimal value is a sequence of characters "0" .. "9", which possibly a minus "-" sign precedes negative numbers to be specified. Examples: 1, 100, -12, 1024

2B. Hexadecimal ($1)

A hexadecimal value consists of the characters "A" .. "F" (or "a" .. "f" with preceding "$" sign. Examples: $FC, $DFF180, -$ABCD

2C. Binary (%1)

Binary numbers begin with a "%" sign and otherwise exist only from "1" and "0". Examples: %111, %1010100001, -%10101

2D glide point (1.0)

Gliding Point Numbers Differ from Normal Decimal Numbers only by the "." sign separating their two sections. One The two sections can be omitted, not both. Note that that glide point numbers represent another internal 32-bit (FFP) representation possession. Chapter 12 contains more information about glide point pay. Examples: 3.14159, .1 (=0.1), 1. (=1.0)

2E. Sign ("a")

The value of a sign (included in double "" quotation- sign) is its ASCII amount, e.g. "A" = 65. In E, immediate character values are a string with up to 4 characters, e.g. "FORM", where the first character "F" the MSB of the 32bit "M" is the LSB (least significant byte).

2F. Character string ('bla')

Strings consist of a sequence of ascii characters included in '' are. The value of such a string is a pointer to its first Signs. Example: 'bla' produces a 32-bit pointer that shows a memory area in which the bytes "b", "l" and "a" are find. ALL strings in E end with a zero byte ("0"). Strings can be format characters that are initiated with a slash "\" are contained. Either to bring in signs from some are unrepresentable for a reason or for use in string- formatting functions such as WriteF(), TextF(), and StringF(), or kick2 VprintF().

\n a line feed (ascii 10)
\a or ''an apostrophe'' (The one that also includes strings)
Escape (ascii 27)
\t tab (ascii 9)
A backslash
0 is a zero byte. Rarely used as ALL strings end with 0
\b a wagon return (ascii 13)

Additionally, when used in formatting functions:

\d print a decimal number
\h print a hexadecimal number
Printing a string
\c Printing a character
\z Set the fill-up byte to '0' characters
format to the left side of the field
Format to the right side of the field

The following field identifiers can follow \d, \h and \s:

[x] Define the exact field size x
(x,y) Set minimum size x and maximum size y (strings only)

Example: Printing a hexadecimal number with 8 digits and zeros at the beginning:

Number: = $ff
WriteF('\z\h[8]\n',number)

results in $000000ff

A string can extend over several lines if the individual Parts are connected with a '+' sign and a <lf>.

'This extra long string' +
'Hooked up over two lines'

2G. Lists ([1,2,3]) and Type Lists

An immediate list is the counterpart of the LIST datatypes, just as 'string' is the counterpart to the STRING or ARRAY OF CHAR datatype. Example:

[3,2,1,4]

is an expression that as a value a pointer to an already initialized has a list. A list in its memory representation is compatible with ARRAY OF LONG, with some additional length information at a negative offset. You can use these immediate lists anywhere where a function a pointer to a field of 32bit values or a list expected. Examples:

['string',1.0.2.1]
[WA FLAGS,1,WA IDCMP,$200,WA WIDTH,120,WA HEIGHT,150,TAG DONE]

The sub-chapter on list functions provides further information on immediate type lists.

EXPRESSIONS

  • A. Format
  • B. Priority and summary
  • C. Types of expression
  • D. Function calls

Previous Chapter Next Chapter

3A. Format

An expression is a piece of source code composed of operators, functions, and brackets, and gives a value.

Expressions consist mainly of:

  • Immediate values, as described in chapter 2
  • Operators, as described in Chapter 4
  • Function calls, as described in chapter 3D
  • brackets (), as described in chapter 3B
  • Variables or variable expressions (see 3C)

Examples of expressions:

1
'Hello'
$ABCD+(2*6)+Abs(a)
(a<1) OR (b>=100)

3B. Priority and summary

Amiga E has no priority bill or anything similar. The This means that expressions are evaluated from left to right. You can do that. by embedding (partial) expressions avoid:

1+2*3 /* =9 */ 1+(2*3) /* =7 */ 2*3+1 /* =7 */

3C. Expressions

There are different types of expression that are used for different purposes. can be used:

  • <var>, consisting of only one variable
  • <varexp>, consisting of a variable, possibly with unary operators,
  • Like ++ (increase) or [] (Field Operator). Further information is available
  • in chapters 4D and 4G. <varexp> makes variable expressions possible,
  • Just like Lvalues in C.
  • Note that these (unary) operators do not take precedence over others.
  • have operators.
  • <exp>. Includes <var> and <varexp> and any other expression.

3D. Function calls

A function call represents an interruption of the current source code in which a function is initiated. This can either be a self-written function (PROC), or a function that is transferred from the system to It will be made available. A function call consists of the function name, followed by zero to infinite many arguments in two brackets () are included and separated from commas ",". Note that the arguments of a function are again expressions. Chapter 6 says how to create your own functions, Chapter 9 and 10 show the installed functions. Examples:

my function(1,2)
Gadget(buffer,glist,2,0,40,80+offset,100,'Cancel')
Close(handle)

14.OBJECT ORIGINATED PROGRAMMING

Since OOP is not yet installed, it cannot be documented will become.

Some theory

OBJECT gauss
com Add(a)
com Sub(a)
com Mul(a)
com Div(a)
com Real2Gauss(a,b)
com LaengeSqr()
com Letter(a)
ENDOBJECT

The largest "normal" number range is the real number range. Most will certainly know what in mathematics a Root means (root(9) = 3 | 3 * 3 = 9 ). In the real number range However, there are also negative numbers whose roots are NOT can be calculated (root(-9) = ? | -3 * 3 = -9 ). However, this only applies to the number range R (real numbers). Gauss (the one from our banknotes ;-) simply has a new Number range invented, which he called the complex numbers. This range of numbers C is based on the following definition:

The following applies to the number i in the number range C: i*i =−1.

(Was not strictly mathematical, but says the most important!)

From this it follows for the root -9:

Root(-9) = 3*i | (3*i) * (3*i) = (3*3) * (i*i) = 9 * -1 = -9 .

(Factors in a product may be reversed: commutative law)

A complex number always has the following format:

Gaussian form: z = a + b*i

(a:Real part / b:Imaginary part).

The real numbers are all contained in the complex numbers. For it applies: b=0.

At some point, someone came up with the idea of changing the Gausian number form differently. presented:

b Polar form : z = Z * ( cos(d)+i*sin(d) )
| z
{ | /| Z = length of the pointer
{ | / | d = Angle between axis a and pointer
Z*sin(d) { | Z/ |
{ | | | | | | | | | | | |
{ | | | | | | | | | | | |
{ |/d)   |   a
| | | |
Z*cos(d)

In order to show that both shapes are identical, the following reshapings:

z = Z * ( cos(d) + i * sin(d) ): polar form

z = Z * cos(d) + Z * sin(d) * i

cos(d) = a/Z and sin(d) = b/Z

z = Z * a/Z + Z * b/Z * i = a + b * i : Gausian form .

I have not yet integrated the polar form in the module, since I have Don't need it yet.

Difference from the predecessor

Differences between 'fifo' and 'stack'

OBJECT fifo or stack
sta Array()
sta Write()
sta Read()
sta Delete()
sta Clear()
sta Exist()
sta Pop() [at 'fifo']
sta Pop() [for 'stack']
sta Push()
ENDOBJECT

Version 1.0: First version

Version 1.1 : Method sta Delete has been added.

This module contains two objects: fifo and stack. Both are Almost identical. The only difference is in the method sta Pop(). Each object generates a dynamic list, It can be treated like an array. But you can also as LIFO (STACK) or FIFO memory.

Call...: ptr.sta Array(num)

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO (fifo|stack). <num> is an integer.

Function..: Creates a list containing <num> cells. This list It can be used like an array. See also: sta Read() and sta Write().

Call....: ptr.sta Write(element,value)

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO (fifo|stack). <element> is an integer while <value> is any It can have content.

Function..: This method describes the <element>.th element with the Value <value>. ATTENTION: You also start from 0 here. See also sta Read().

Call....: value := ptr.sta Read(element)

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO (fifo|stack). <element> is an integer while <value> is the receives the function value.

Function..: This method lists from the element <element> and delivers the function value as a result (<value>). See also sta Write().

Call...: ptr.sta Clear()

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO (fifo|stack).

Function..: The complete dynamic list is deleted. This function is also called by the respective destructor, which is why they is needed only in special cases.

Call...: bool := ptr.sta Exist()

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO (fifo|stack).

Function..: If the list contains at least 1 element, the Variable <bool> the value TRUE, otherwise FALSE.

Call....: value := ptr.sta Pop()

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO fifo.

Function..: This method provides the value of the 1st element of the Chain <ptr> back as a result. This first element It will be immediately deleted. Contrast: sta Pop() OF stack

Call....: value := ptr.sta Pop()

Parameter.: <ptr> is of type PTR TO fifo.

Function..: This method provides the value of the last element of the Chain <ptr> back as a result. This last element It will be immediately deleted. Contrast: sta Pop() OF fifo

Call...: ptr.sta Push(value)

Parameter.: <ptr> is a variable of type PTR TO (fifo|stack). <value> is any number.

Function..: This method creates a new node with the content <value>. This node will always reach the end of the chain <ptr> hanged.

Call...: ptr.sta Delete(num)

Parameter.: <ptr> is a variable of type PTR TO (fifo|stack). <num> is an element of this list.

Function..: The <num>.th element of the list <ptr> is deleted, where the list begins with the index 0.

Introduction:

What exactly is Ber? BER is a program useful for civil servants can be. It calculates the anniversary on a date, e.g. 1.1 is the 1 anniversary; Of course, it can also do so in the opposite direction.

To convert a date into an anniversary you only need to click the button Date -> Anniversary to press and answer the questions of the program And you get the usually correct result. In any case, Over time, all errors have been corrected and it could possibly an error occurs in new functions. This should be thanks to the Betatesters no longer occur!

However, if errors occur, please contact me. (Address see SOFTINFO)

Features of BER:

  • Font sensitive
  • quickly in his calculations
  • Relatively small binary files
  • StyleGuide compliant

Conditions:

  • ReqTools.library (at least version 37+)
  • DOS 2.xx or higher
  • a fast processor would not be bad, but
  • not required -> 68020 +
  • at least 90 KB of free memory

Use:

BER should be easy to use. The GUI (Graphics User Interface) from BER StyleGuide is compliant.

The surface:

Anniversary -> Date Information
Date -> Anniversary End

Show the month as a name
o Calculation for leap year

The theory of BER:

A year is divided into 365 days, 52 (actually 53) weeks and 12 months. Each week has 7 days; You can convert anniversaries into weeks.

Calculation of weeks:

Label:
IF Anniversary<7 ; When the loop is at the end, the
Month: = Month + 1 ; week counted and the result is
ELSE; the week in which the anniversary is.
Anniversary - 7
Month: = Moant + 1
JUMP label ; Jump to start to get loop
ENDIF

The calculation of the week is based simply on the fact that a week is 7 days You have, and you do that with a loop where you always have 7 days from deducts the anniversary and adds a week to the weeks the week receives, in which is the anniversary.

Calculation of the anniversary:

The calculation of the anniversary is a bit more complicated. You have to be for everyone Month have a kind of mask, after which the different data is evaluated will become.

The calculation is simply based on the fact that each month a fixed number of has days. This number is used as a sum so as not to be extra for each Month to calculate the number of days in the program. So it's based on of the month, less 1, the number of elapsed days is calculated, and then Add the date (day) and then you get the anniversaries.

Calculation of the date:

The calculation of the date is based on the calculation of the anniversary in reverse order. But here the calculation is much more complex. You have a different number of days for each month. So it becomes a The number of days in which the number of days Subtract the corresponding month until you have only a number of days left that No longer big enough to take another month off. Then you have this the result of the day, and one must subtract for each month (as days) Add a month. The result is then the date

Art .............: Help for speed reading data
Author ...........: Jörg Wach

Documentation ReadStrBuf

What is ReadStrBuf?

ReadStrBuf is a small program that I wrote After the loading times of my program Scancode more likely to have moved to sleep (see also) Scancode.doc. The real problem was the ReadStr routine. This routine is a standard routine of Amiga e, but unfortunately it is No routine!! What is called buffeted here? Now, when you read it, not only the desired number of A number of bytes, but a number of bytes. (usually 512 bytes). What is the nonsense, now some will think. Well, if your program should read all the characters individually, so it would always first write the instruction to the Trackdisk.Device, this performs a one-time reading and returns the characters. and If you want to read 512 characters, the routine will be 512 times. Executed! :-( But the buffet reading is only done once and you have 512 characters in memory. Then the reading of the individual characters no longer from the disk, but from the Memory and that goes a lot faster. A pro pro fast if the 512 characters are read should be a intelligent routine of course read the next 512 characters.

Features of GetArgs

In the routine itself you can set a free buffer. I have also tried some values, but from a buffer size from 2K does not bring much additional speed. Otherwise, this should only be an example of how Such a routine could look like ;-

Call, handover parameters

Readstrbuf is called from the CLI without transfer parameters Started directly from the workbench. It reads its own source code and outputs it on the screen (What a speed). Try the same with ReadStr!

Source code explanation

Is (hopefully) due to my comments in the source self-explanatory.

Other

Especially in order to maintain compatibility with the "old" OS one should Use this proc. As of OS 2.0, the Dos has its own standard Procedures for buffeted reading and writing are available.

Copyrights

Don't do it.

Documentation GetArgs

What is GetArgs?

Getargs should give you an example of how to use Amiga E You can do command line parsing. A special one for this This command is (unfortunately) missing in Amiga E.

Since I myself the command line in my program Scancode I still have to evaluate the program OS 1.2/1.3 I had to keep compatible on the two small progs came for the evaluation.

Features of GetArgs

Getargs determined

  • how many arguments have been submitted
  • and
  • shows them in order.

Not very much? Well, if you have a corresponding order (as in C or PCQ) certainly. But once you have a Need to tinker. It is certainly helpful to everyone else.

Call, handover parameters

GetArgs cannot be accessed via the Workbench (wg. Args indication.

Getargs is called with any number of arguments. E.g.

Getargsehne mene muh

Getargs then gives out:

Arguments: 3
1st argument = stretch.
2nd argument = mehne.
3rd argument = muh.

Et voila, that wars!

Author: Daniel van Gerpen

Description of side-faces

You know the many smils who are in it. There are letters that we all send to each other.

So what can you make of it? Right, write a program in E, that ALL possible combinations that exist are expressed once.

I have not seen such a program.

I do not want to argue with anyone about sense or nonsense. I But this thing is really great. What do many of the little ones say? Faces off? Maybe someone will dare to write a description. ran.

Jörg.

Side faces

Show you the wonderful world of 8's, B^o's and :^}'s...

Toss, see, amaze...

Who made more than 210 (!!) pieces???

DEF i,j,k,c=0

PROC main()
FOR i = 1 TO 5
FOR j = 1 TO 3
FOR k = 1 TO 14
Draw()
ENDFOR
ENDFOR
ENDFOR
ENDPROC


PROC draw()
SELECT i
CASE 1; WriteF(':')
CASE 2; WriteF('8')
CASE 3; WriteF(';')
CASE 4; WriteF('|')
CASE 5; WriteF('ß')

ENDSELECTIVE
SELECTIVE j
CASE 1; WriteF('-')
CASE 2; WriteF('')
CASE 3; WriteF('^')
ENDSELECTIVE
SELECTIVE K
CASE 1; WriteF(')'
CASE 2; WriteF('(')
CASE 3; WriteF('|')
CASE 4; WriteF('>')
CASE 5; WriteF('<')
CASE 6; WriteF('}')
CASE 7; WriteF('{')
CASE 8; WriteF(') '
CASE 9; WriteF('[')
CASE 10; WriteF('+')
CASE 11; WriteF('*')
CASE 12; WriteF('X')
CASE 13; WriteF('C')
CASE 14; WriteF('7')
ENDSELECTIVE
IF c++>3
WriteF('\n\n')
c: = 0
ENDIF
ENDPROC

The program CountTYPEs serves for comfortable counting of all "TYPE" defi- nition in a FileTypes file. Both "TYPE" display and counters can also be (de)activated independently of one another.

CountTYPEs was written with AmigaE 2.1b (hence the - unnecessary - Open some libraries) and is available from OS 2.04 (V37) on all Amiga min. 512 kB of RAM running.

ATTENTION: in order for the program to run correctly, you must meet the following conditions- Note:

  • the program is for a max. Line length of 255 characters.
  • One line should therefore NEVER be longer (crash danger!!).
  • every "TYPE" must be at the beginning of a line, otherwise it will not
  • counted. Just look at the FileTypes file because it
  • It already has the right structure.
  • every "TYPE" must be written in capital letters. "Type" or "Type"
  • Do not count.
  • the counting process can be subtracted by the key combination <Ctrl c>
  • breaking.
  • the program is reentrant and can be loaded resident (pure).

The CountTYPEs call is as follows:

CountTYPEs <FileTypes file> [-st] [-nc]

If CountTYPEs is called without parameters, a short overview appears.

<FileTypes file> specifies the file that opens before counting. The file must have the structure described in NewDir.guide and "Introduction" have.

-st activates the display of the "TYPE"s. First of all, the current row number and the corresponding row. In addition, the parameter -nc is specified, the output of the current row number is neglected.

-nc activates the automatically displayed counter that is currently the bear- indicates the middle line.

The call of MegaConvert is as simple as anything: simple Double-click the icon or enter the program name into a shell! The following tool types are possible in the icon (ATTENTION: in the case of the unregister-) In this version, the ToolTypes are ignored!!

HELPFILE=<path to this guide>

Specifies which AmigaGuide file is printed on <Help> or dial of the Menu item “Help...” should be loaded. The path should be commo- dores recommendations on “HELP:German/MegaConvert.guide” are. Default: HELP:German/MegaConvert.guide

LVOFORMAT=<Format string for LVO generation>

specifies how the output in the convert mode "FD file --> assembler" has to look. The following format characters can be displayed as often as desired. are used:

%[<l>]f adds the name of the library function (without " LVO"). It
It is possible to use a max. 2 digit length. Is the
String shorter than this length, it becomes to the right with blank lines
It is filled, otherwise it will only be inserted.
%[<l>]F as %f, but left-handed filling
%[<l>]o inserts the decimal offset of the function (with leading
"-". See %f fill up.
%[<l>]O as %o, but left-handed filling
%[<l>]h inserts the hexadecimal offset of the function (with leading)
"-$". Make up see %f
%[<l>]H as %h, but left filling
%[<a>]t adds tab characters. If the maximum 2 digit number
<a> TABs are inserted, otherwise only 1.
Example: "%tLIBDEF%t LVO%5f%t;%6O"
Default : LIBDEF  LVO%f

KEEPAGLIB=YES|NO

Specifies whether the amigaguide.library should be kept in memory. If “NO”, the library will immediately after closing AmigaGuide, which appears when the menu item “Help ..” is selected, closed. See also: In the event of a lack of memory, the “Avail FLUSH” shell input can be used. from the memory. Do you have your workbench with “LoadWB” -debug", is also the workbench menu item "Debug/flushlibs" possible. Default: “NO”

CONWIN=<Window specification>

Specifies the position and size of the CON: window that is displayed when E- Modules are used. The information should have the following format: "CONWIN=CON:<left edge>/<upper edge>/<width>/<height>/". To the String is attached "Show E-modulus on .." Of course, instead of CON: also an identifier of one of the common CON: substitutes is used (Example: GMC:0/11/640/245/). Default: CON:0/11/640/189/

PUBSCREEN=<Name of a PublicScreen>

Specifies on which PublicScreen the MegaConvert window and all Other windows and requesters should be opened. Default: “Workbench”

Could MegaConvert be started without error, is immediately the user- surface visible. There are a number of gadgets here. Furthermore, There is a menu.

And this is how converting one file to another goes on:

  • first select the type of the source and the destination file,
  • now you select the source and destination file by keyboard or file requester,
  • via menu, gadget or keyboard you now start the conversion.

Now follows an explanation of the functions that emanate from each gadget. The keyboard shortcuts are indicated in brackets.

left string gadget

is used to specify the source file. This must have a different name than the have target file.

Right string gadget

is used to indicate the destination file. This must have a different name than the have a source file.

left cycle gadget

Activate the type of source file

Right cycle gadget

Activate the target file type

"Starting." (s)

starts the conversion process. In the conversion modes "FD file -->" E-Module" and "C-Pragma --> E-Module" appears a string requester, in which enters the complete file name (e.g. "cx.library") of the library We must. ATTENTION: in the unregistered version, in all conversion modes only max. 20 lines converted!!

“Stop...” (q)

terminates MegaConvert (with security query)

This overview lists all menu items of MegaConvert and their radio tions. In brackets are the keyboard shortcuts, which together with <Amiga right> must be pressed.

Menu »Project«:

"Info..."

Issues some communications about MegaConvert

“Info about registration...”

gives some notices about the registration status of the used sion from

"Source file..." (<o>)

calls a file requester with which the source file is selected- It can. This must have a different name than the target file. The Path of the file then appears in the left string gadget.

"Destination file..." (<d>)

Calls a file requester that selects the destination file can. This must have a different name than the source file. The path The file will appear in the right string gadget.

"Start conversion..." (<s>)

starts the conversion process. In the conversion modes "FD file -->" E-Module" and "C-Pragma --> E-Module" appears a string requester, in which enters the complete file name (e.g. "cx.library") of the library We must. ATTENTION: in the unregistered version, in all conversion modes only max. 20 lines converted!!

"Show E-Module..." (<m>)

Calls a file requester that selects an AmigaE module It can be displayed then. First, you can determine whether the output into a window ("CON:") or into a file ("File.") Want to redirect. If you select the file, a file-reque- ster. "Cancel" stops the process. Tip to "CON:": if the output goes beyond the lower window edge, is it is helpful to use the right mouse button or the key combination <Alt right Press Amiga right> to stop the output (the keys are there) To hold on, of course. ATTENTION: the redirection to a file is in the unregistered version Blocked!!

“Help...” (<h>, <help> without <Amiga right>)

loads first, if necessary & possible, the amigaguide.library and shows this guidance. If an error occurs, nothing happens! ATTENTION: this feature is locked in the unregistered version !!

“Stop...” (q)

terminates MegaConvert (with security query)

Menu "Preferences"

“LVO format string...”

is used for subsequent modification of the LVO format string. It appears that String requester in which the string can be changed.

FD file --> E-module

For this conversion mode, a text file must be present, the following may contain lines. Empty lines are not allowed, comments are made with "*" and may be in any line. Except in Com- mentars must not appear spaces in the entire file.

##base <Name of Library-Base>

  • must occur once and before the first function,
  • specifies the name of the library base (usually with leading " ", should be on
  • "Base" ends,
  • Example: ##base ExampleBase

##bias <LVO for the first function>

  • must occur only once and before the first function,
  • specifies the LVO for the first function (positive; always 30),
  • Example: ##bias 30

<Name of function>(<Name of parameters>)(<Register of parameters>)

  • may occur several times, but only after "##base .." and "##bias ..",
  • Gives the name of the Jew. function, the names of the parameters of the function
  • and register the parameters,
  • Example: Example Function(Parameter1,Parameter2)(a0,a1)

##public

  • may occur several times, but only after "##base .." and "##bias ..",
  • indicates that all of the following functions are released for use,

##private

  • may occur several times, but only after "##base .." and "##bias ..",
  • indicates that all of the following functions are blocked for use
  • (APPLAUTION: MegaConvert creates a locked function that can be used in this
  • Cannot be used!!

##end

  • must occur once and at the end of the file,
  • Specifies the end of the file.

Another word about "##public" and "##private": by default, "##public" is So it wouldn't be necessary for either of them if all of them functions of the jew. library are released for use. Nevertheless, not missed, at least directly before the first function Writing "##public". This increases the clarity and dismisses the understandings out of the way.

Please also see the file "Example lib.fd" in the directory "Examples."

C-Pragma --> Module of E

For this conversion mode, there must be a text file from which all Lines other than the following are ignored:

#pragma libcall <Name of library base> <Name of function> <1> <2>

  • may occur several times,
  • 1: LVO to this function (positive, hexadecimal),
  • 2 shows the registers of the parameters of the function,
  • specifies the name of the library base (should end in "base"),
  • indicates the name of the function,
  • specifies the LVO for this function,
  • specifies the registers of the parameters of this function,
  • Example: #pragma libcall ExampleBase ExampleFunction 1e 9802

Please also see the file "Example pragma.h" in the directory "Examples."

FD file --> Assembly

For this conversion mode, a "FD file --> E-module" must be described There is a text file. MegaConvert generates an assembler- Include, whose appearance you can determine with the LVO format string.

Unfortunately, that is all I can tell you in this brief. Please Procure yourself therefore elsewhere literature, because anyone who is serious programmed, should be clear about above mentioned construction forms.

Errors can occur both during start and during program execution. Start errors are basically displayed in a requester, wherein these also lead to the termination of the program. Execution error in contrast MegaConvert is displayed in a requester. Despite these mistakes You can continue working normally.

Start error messages

"Couldn't get context!"

the memory for the gadgets could not be obtained

"Couldn't create gadgets!"

the gadgets could not be created

"Couldn't lock pubscreen!"

a temporary lock on the desired PublicScreen could not are concerned;

"Couldn't get VisualInfos!"

the VisualInfos of the Workbench could not be obtained

"Couldn't open gadtools.library 37 !!"

gadtools.library (minimum version 37) could not be opened

"Couldn't open window!"

The window could not be opened

"Couldn't create menus!"

The menu could not be created

"Couldn't open reqtools.library 38 !!"

the reqtools.library (minimum version 38) could not be opened

"Couldn't allocate file requester!!"

the memory for the file requester could not be obtained

"Couldn't get AmigaGuide memory!"

the memory for the amigaguide.library could not be obtained

"Couldn't open icon.library 34!"

icon.library (minimum version 34) could not be opened

Documentation Scancode

Do you feel the same way? Something animal annoys you and you Want to change it? For example, you must always consider which assembly command Now the faster one or if you still have your ace code Can you optimize? I think I have the right thing for you!

The solution is called SCANCODE!!!

What is Scancode?

Scancode examines assembler source and gives the assembly source with the associated clock cycles.

This only applies to valid 68000 commands.

In addition, Scancode has a direct dialog makes it possible to directly reduce the corresponding number of clock cycles. Questions. More on that later.

Features of Scancode

Scan code can be

Determine ALL clock cycles for ALL 68000 commands, no matter with which addressing type or with which operands.

Scancode also detects variables or constants used and can also use the correct number of clock cycles Identify!

- Scancode can, controlled by options, according to the commands spend rte, rtr, rts, jmp, jsr or bxx subtotals (Especially useful if only sections or under- Optimize programs.

Scancode detects invalid 68000 commands and This is a quick help for source verification.

- Scancode also detects commands where not specified has been addressed whether it has been LONG, WORD or BYTE are. Scancode assumes that either the command is only allowed in a single addressing type (e.g. MULU is always WORD) or is determined from the command table the first entry of the command, which (Mostly) byte.

I would therefore point out that it is clear to everyone that:

Unless SAUBER has been programmed, Scrap out!

- Scancode can translate source, which in

  • DEVPAC
  • — METACOMCO
  • A68K

format is available (others were not available to me for testing) Decision.

Scancode has a dialog interface that allows Then, enter the commands and then enter the commands. Display the number of clock cycles directly on the screen. This is especially important when you're thinking, which command construction is the faster.

- Scancode is poisonware, so damn cheap.

- Scancode is the only program that can be used for this (to The current date (16.11.1992) is!

Scan code cannot be

- Translate commands to the 68010, 68020, 68030 or 68040 CPU (if there are any?).

- Assembler-Source format correctly, if in this Tabs (not looking so nice right now).

- is (yet) not particularly fast (see also section) "Times".

- does not specify the number of clock cycles for the following commands Unconditionally correct again:

---> asl, asr, lsl, lsr, rol, ror, roxl, roxr,

And why not? Because in these orders the number of Clock cycles depend on how many bits shall be. And I can't figure that out if I do this with the contents of a register!

Scancode takes an average value that is not necessarily must be consistent with actual circumstances. Unfortunately, I could not think of anything better.

So you see, Scancode isn't bad at all. Especially for them, who want to let off steam in assembler for the first time, is Scancode is a great help. But also with the so-called freaks Scancode can be a help. I have noticed over and over again that some of the Make great programs, but the execution time is still essential- could be optimized. I count myself among them!

But how do you do that without an appropriate tool? Do they?

Well, now you have one!!

Call, handover parameters

Scancode can be called ONLY in the CLI.

For this purpose, the call is made as follows:

SCANCODE Option(s) Source [Destination]

Option(s):

Scancode is expected. One option! If you do not You get an error message.

Options may include:

? ---> Provides a short help text.
b ---> creates a subtotal behind each bxx.
j ---> creates an intermediate
total.
r ---> creates behind each rts, rtr and rte
Subtotal.
t ---> should not be used under any circumstances!
It only serves my test. If
But it still enters .... itself to blame!
Then you can enter in the meantime.
Scancode works, put on a cup of coffee
And wait!

So far as the options you have in the so-called. Use batch can. A prerequisite for this is an input file then outputs the scan code with the addition ".TAKT" or A file you have chosen.

The options can be entered in any order.

Do you like examples?

OK:

Scan code jr MeinAssCode

---> Scancode reads the file "MyAssCode" and gives the file "MyAssCode.TAKT". For each JSR, JMP, RTR, RTS and RTE Subtotals issued.

Scancode rb MeinAssCode Dummy

---> Scancode reads the file "MyAssCode" and gives file "Dummy". It is used in every RTR, RTS and Bxx. Subtotals are issued.

Scancode MeinAssCode Dummy

---> Scancode outputs a help text!

These are the examples.

Now comes the cream candy:

If you call scan code with the option "d", then into direct dialogue.

For this purpose, the input in the CLI must look as follows:

Scan code d

That's wars!

Now, what does direct dialogue mean?

Nothing other than that you enter the commands and scancode Tell you how many clock cycles it uses.

Integration into own programmes

Damn bad, believe me, damn bad.

Periods

Think about it, the Amiga rages so with about 7.09 Mhz through the area. This means that a clock cycle Roundabout 141 nanoseconds consumed.

Of course, this is already a dream value, because then you would all have to Turn off Interupts, Task Switchings, etc., and what will benefit you then Still your Amiga?

But not bad as an indication. So you should have them. Calculate program routines.

Scancode itself rages, at least with me (and I have a damned one) slow disk, at a source of 546 lines and all switched on options in 12 seconds; including the creation of new file.

With only one option, it takes 11 seconds, so not so Insanely less.

I call that slow. In a newer version I'm going to rewrite the spreadsheet, the idea of how, I already have.

The Golden Proggi Rules

Well, so especially for beginners it is in the large selection of 68000er It is difficult to use the right commands. So I have Let's put together some tips on how to make programs faster. can (does not claim to be complete!):

Use the "Quick" commands!

If possible, you should always moveq, addq or subq Prefer.

Moveq fills you in 4 (!) clock cycles comprising: a signed number in 8-bit format (+ 127 to) - 128. The registry is extended to LONG.

Addq and Subq very quickly subtract values from 1 to 8 They are much faster than the comparable Commands ADDI or SUBI.

ASL, ASR, LSR, LSL before Mulx or Divx at powers of 2.

If you have a value of 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 Multiply or divide, so do not use the MULx or DIVx commands. The bit shift commands are much faster in this area.

Anything about it, however, you should already be with the MULx or DIVx commands, even if you have a few Smart things to say otherwise!

The clock cycle specifications for these two commands are namely MAXIMUM VALUES and if I look at the data description of the 68000er did not read, you can read everything else about this Run both commands faster (or has someone else) Info?

Avoid the CLR.L command!

I still see that some Heinis write --- clr.l D0 --- with not to be disregarded 6 clock cycles. Moveq is simply 2 clock cycles faster.

And address registers, despite opinions to the contrary, Do not delete it!

What else should be missed with clr.x?

Look at the following list:

---> clr.l $471111 = 28 clock cycles

Alternative:

moveq.l #0,d0 = 4 clock cycles
move.l d0,$471111 = 20 clock cycles
---> Savings: 4 clock cycles

Something thought about the "curve", but faster.

LEA is also an order!

And no slower! With some addressing (e.g. 8-bit offset with addition, so something like LEA $33(a0,d0),a1) This command is much faster and shorter than comparable orders. It should also be used.

So whoever thinks "oh just because of the few clock cycles" Such an insurrection should be pointed out, which is subprograms, which are run 200 times per pass, for example, at least with 4 clock cycles time saving by another program- mation 800 clock cycles can be saved, or relative to to express, 112.8 MiKrosekunden (in the best case) saved Become!

This is a damn long time for the Amiga!!!

If you have other similar clever tips in stock, these Just for the beginners, publish.

The Golden Proggi Rules

Well, so especially for beginners it is in the large selection of 68000er It is difficult to use the right commands. So I have Let's put together some tips on how to make programs faster. can (does not claim to be complete!):

Use the "Quick" commands!

If possible, you should always moveq, addq or subq Prefer.

Moveq fills you in 4 (!) clock cycles comprising: a signed number in 8-bit format (+ 127 to) - 128. The registry is extended to LONG.

Addq and Subq very quickly subtract values from 1 to 8 They are much faster than the comparable Commands ADDI or SUBI.

Even commands like "Move.l #10,address" forget very quickly. The command requires 10 bytes and 28 clock cycles. Better go with:

moveq #10,d0 ---> 2 bytes and 4 cycles
move.l d0,address ---> 6 bytes and 20 cycles.
Savings: 2 bytes and 4 clock cycles.

Or how about with

cmp.l #5,d0 ---> 6 bytes and 14 cycles

replaced by:

moveq #5,d1 ---> 2 bytes and 4 cycles
cmp.l d1,d0 ---> 2 bytes and 6 cycles.

Savings: 2 bytes and 4 cycles.

Even if the limits for the Quick command are exceeded (+127 to -128) you can also up to the values 256 quite a bit Save time, as you can see here:

move.l #129,d0 ---> 6 bytes and 12 cycles

replaced by:

moveq #256-129,d0 ---> 2 bytes and 4 cycles
neg d0 ---> 2 bytes and 4 cycles.

Savings: 2 bytes and 4 cycles.

ASL, ASR, LSR, LSL before Mulx or Divx at powers of 2.

If you have a value of 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 Multiply or divide, so do not use the MULx or DIVx commands. The bit shift commands are much faster in this area.

Anything about it, however, you should already be with the MULx or DIVx commands, even if you have a few Smart things to say otherwise!

The clock cycle specifications for these two commands are namely MAXIMUM VALUES and if I look at the data description of the 68000er did not read, you can read everything else about this Run both commands faster (or has someone else) Info?

Avoid the CLR.L command!

I still see that some Heinis write --- clr.l D0 --- with not to be disregarded 6 clock cycles. Moveq is simply 2 clock cycles faster.

And address registers, despite opinions to the contrary, Do not delete it!

What else should be missed with clr.x?

Look at the following list:

---> clr.l $471111 = 28 clock cycles

Alternative:

moveq.l #0,d0 = 4 clock cycles
move.l d0,$471111 = 20 clock cycles

---> Savings: 4 clock cycles

Something thought about the "curve", but faster.

LEA is also an order!

And no slower! With some addressing (e.g. 8-bit offset with addition, so something like LEA $33(a0,d0),a1) This command is much faster and shorter than comparable orders. It should also be used.

For example, the following commands should be replaced by Lea:

- movea.l #1974,a0 ---> 6 bytes and 12 cycles

replace by:

lea 1974,a0 ---> 4 bytes and 8 clock cycles.

Savings: 2 bytes and 4 cycles.

- movea.l a0,a1 ---> 2 bytes and 4 cycles
adda.l #1974,a1 ---> 6 bytes and 14 cycles

replace by:

lea 1974(a0),a1 ---> 4 bytes and 8 cycles.

Savings: 4 bytes and 10(!) Cycles.

So whoever thinks "oh just because of the few clock cycles" Such an insurrection should be pointed out, which is subprograms, which are run 200 times per pass, for example, at least with 4 clock cycles time saving by another program- 800 cycles can be saved!

This is a damn long time for the Amiga!!!

If you have other similar clever tips in stock, these Just for the beginners, publish.
