GadToolsBox (Jaba Development) is a program that Programmer allows graphic surfaces to be drawn and in a special format. The resulting GUI file does not contain any source code, but only the Description of the surface. Here come the so-called source text- Generators come into play whose task is to put the GUI file in converting source code. Also for E there is such a Source code generator called "SrcGen", created by the programmer of this language (Wouter van Oortmerssen). Of course, he does not have that much time in this source code generator can stick, as in his language, which is why the result It was passable but not intoxicating. This is why I wrote a source code generator myself, which has some additional functions and over a simple graphical user interface.

Absolutely necessary:

  • Amiga OS 2.04 or higher
  • About 250 KB of free main memory
  • "gadtoolsbox.library" v35 or higher
  • "nofrag.library" v2.2 or higher

Should there be:

  • Compiler Amiga-E v3.0 or higher
  • GadToolsBox v2.0c or higher
  • (Perhaps older versions also work :)
  • powerpacker.library v35.347 or higher
  • "asl.library" v37 or higher

The libraries listed in "System Requirements" should in the directory "Libs:". The E-modules should in the directory "EModules:GTS/" are located around the generated compile source code. The position of the program and Documentation does not matter.

Function: This method initializes the data components of the object and stores the current color values of the Screens <2> to restore them after change to be able to.

Syntax...: <1> := <2>.col ColoraExist()
<1>: is a Boolean value
<2>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'

Function: This Boolean method provides the value TRUE if the Color palette of the old screen to be stored could. Without this security copy of the pallet, refused the object its service.

Syntax...: <1>.col FreeColora()
<1>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'

Function: This method deletes the backup copy of the color palette, which in this case is destroyed. This method shall be: automatically called by the destructor end().

Syntax...: <1>.col Restore()
<1>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'

Function.: During initialization using col InitColora() a security copy of the color palette is prepared which is restored with this call.

PRIVATE METHODE (unfortunately I can not hide)

Syntax...: <1>.col Shift(<2>,<3>,<4>)
<1>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'
<2>: is the number of rotations performed
<3>: is either COL COL or COL CYCLUS, the latter
ensures that a rotation on the whole pallet
Relating to
<4>: Waiting time to dampen the "rotation speed"

Function.: This method allows ColorCycling. Does the parameter <3> the value COL COL, <2> colors are rotated, otherwise rotates the entire palette <2> times. <4> is only to make the effect "more pleasant" for the eyes design.

Syntax...: <1>.col SetCols(<2>,<3>,<4>)
<1>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'
<2>: is an e-pointer to a function red(x)
<3>: is an e-pointer to a function green(x)
<4>: is an e-pointer to a function blue(x)

Function: This method creates a new palette for the screen, wherein the color values are calculated. The functions shall: receive the index of the color as a parameter and value, the intensity of the component (red, green, blue) return.

Syntax...: END <1>
<1>: is a variable of type `PTR TO colora'

Function: This method is the so-called destructor and is automatically when the object is deleted.

Author: Daniel Kasmeroglu

Explanations of the printer routines 'printer.e'.

Ante Scriptum:

Good Tach! all together. Below are explanations about those of me written printer routines. Before these routines, I had the 'printer.device' quite a respect (complicated there), but now It has become quite easy to print a text or hard copy. I do not assume any guarantee for correct operation, use on my own Danger! But now quickly to the descriptions...

Function name:

printer open()

This routine does not expect any parameters. It 'opens' the in the Preferences set printer and identifies it in the system as 'occupied', i.e. another program can only access it when it is released by us was (in this case usefully via printer close()). If an error occurs when opening, the return value of the function Set as follows:

( -1 ) - RESERVED (actually error when specifying the unit, but here meaningless [or?] -2 - Error in CreateMsgPort() It was not possible to have a 'message port' ['news port'] set up. For communication within the Operating system is indispensable, unfortunately can not printed. -3 - Error in CreateIORequest() An IORequest is ·the· important structure for devices. It shall: is, among other things, the message port, the unit (for drives: unit=0) -> on DF0 is accessed) and much more is recorded. ··Uncanny·· Important! -4 - Error in OpenDevice() Unlike Libraries, Devices Need to Open already initialized structures, the IORequest and so on. Therefore, only now is OpenDevice() called after everything Others succeeded. If, for example, now no more enough memory is free, it can still lead to an error come. Too bad, but it should be rare.

If the return value is greater than ZERO, no error occurred, this is the the address of the IORequest for access to the printer. She is with them. transferring other printer functions (there is no check whether The truth of this statement, so give the right thing! [now something about the internal procedure, who does not want to know, skips this section By the way, the IORequests for the printing of texts with and without Replacement of escape sequences and for graphic expression in each case different size, but don't worry, you don't have to go three times Open the printer or close it when changing the type of printer and re-open it open - it simply became the largest IORequest from the system (iodrpreq - InputOutputDumpRastPortREQuest [I guess]). The function parameters are now simply defined as LONG if so if you want to access structural elements (ior.command), you have to prior to a correspondingly 'typed' variable (DEF ior:PTR TO iodrpreq) Assign the content of this parameter. Other languages then complain and require a type casting (C), but E does not matter.

Function name:

printer close()

The only parameter of this function is the iodrpreq of printer open(). 'Closes' the printer and logs off the message port, etc. That's what you do. Just so that the system memory does not become too little, huh?

Function name:

printer rawwrite()

Parameters:

ioreq - result of printer open()
zkette - the string to be output
length - the length of the string

The character string is output on the printer. The character string can They also contain escape sequences, they are not replaced. These For example, sequences can be printer-specific commands that are not included in the ANSI standard. While the text is printed, sleeping the task, since working with DoIO() - SendIO() would be asynchronous.

Function name:

printer writer

Parameters:

s. printer rawwrite()

The string is sent to the printer, but here is a Replacement of escape sequences.

Function name:

printer command

Parameters:

ioreq - as before
kommando - number or constant denoting the command
p0-p3 - Parameters 1 to 4 for this command

Looks good, right? This function sends a command to the printer, It can have up to four parameters. Examples:

Printer reset
Command number: 0
Parameter 0: 0
Parameter 1: 0
Parameters 2: 0
Parameter 3: 0

Set left and right margins:
Command number: 65
Parameter 0: 2 /* left edge on 2 */
Parameter 1: 77 /* right 77 */
Parameters 2: 0
Parameter 3: 0

As you can see, unused parameters are usefully set to 0 set.

Function name:

printer graphic dump

Parameters:

ioreq - result of printer open()
rport - the RastPort to be printed
cmap - the ColorMap
vmodes - ViewModes of the screen
srcx, srcy
srcwidth,
srcheight - Dimensions of the neckline: Starting point & width & height
destcols,
destrows - Print width on the printer in points
Special - Special flags

YesHAAAA, this is a fine function, it prints a RastPort Off. As you all know, I don't need to tell you, also a screen a RastPort, therefore you can also simply a whole Print screen content. The ColorMap is just like the ViewModes in the ViewPort of the screen - in the ColorMap are the color values in the ViewModes, what resolution the screen has. Now follow the extent of the section to be printed: first the coordinates of the starting point in the RastPort, then width and height, then the dimensions of the expression (destcols = destination columns =) destination columns; destrows = destination rows = destination rows; where with column Each line means one point! Finally, it is possible via the SPECIAL flag in the Preferences to change the set expression (density, etc.). Put the flag on Zero, stay with the old one. This should be done calmly.

At the end of the year, a complete calendar with all data for documentation.

Conditions

List

The program was only tested on an Amiga 2000 with OS 3.1.

According to the author, there should be no difficulties on other Give Amigas. OS 2.04 is required at least.

In addition, the library is "reqtools.library" by Nico Francois required. This is included in the "LIBS" drawer. Copyright and "DISTRIBUTION" please note!

Installation

List

Copying:

The program by moving the icon or with shell

"Copy dfx:Calendar TO drive:[directory] ALL"

in a list.

Recommendation For a better overview, the program should be included in its own directory. "Calendar" is loaded. In this directory, the files should for the dates and dates also be located. The requirement of the dates and dates is done with "Calendar:Daten.DAT" or "Data". with "Calendar:Terminexxxx.DAT", where for xxxx the requested calendar year is inserted.

User startup: Please insert in the user startup:

Assign Calendar: drive:[directory/]Calendar DEFER

for example:

Assign Calendar DH0:Tools/Calendar DEFER

Reboot Amiga for registration to take effect.

Starting

List

The program runs on the Workbench in Hires (640*256).

Double click in the corresponding drawer "calendar"

The program is loaded.

Prefs

List

In the program is the processing of various forms of the date possible.

In most cases, this data is always the same for a user. That's why "Kalender.Prefs" was created. After cessation of 6 switches "Format|Year|Separation" for dates and dates can be set to position by the pressure on the switch "Prefs".

If the program at the next call in the drawer "calendar" a file "Calendar.Prefs" finds a query whether this file It should not be loaded.

Main programme

List

The surface of the main program consists of fields and buttons:

Calendar type: Monthly forms Monthly forms
Weekly newspapers

Monthly sheets: one month is printed for each A4 sheet.

Weekly sheets: Yes A4 sheet will be printed for three weeks. These can be the lower edge of a field is cut, and The result is a small calendar for writing. table.

for year: By clicking on the input field, the desired year must be

for example: 1995<RETURN>

The "Load appointments" switch is now released.

by: Settlement of the beginning month.

until the end of the month.

Note! If the end month becomes smaller than the beginning month after examination a note is issued. It can only create a calendar for 1 year will become.

Reason: The dates are only for the corresponding. Year valid.

Loading data:

This includes three switches for the format of the data:

Format: [ttmm|mmtt|ttt]
tt=day mm=month ttt=lfd. Anniversary

Year: [..yyyy|yyyy..]
jjjj=year ..=year Following or leading

Separation: [No] Yes
Yes=There are special characters in the chain,
e.g.: . or / when retrieved from databases.

The possibilities see data

An ASL requester is addressed with the “load data” switch, which has specified as path "calendar:" and as file "data.DAT".

In the field below, after loading, the path and the file is displayed.

Loading dates:

As already described under "Load data", only now for appointments. Appointments can only be loaded when the calendar year is entered has been.

HP 500 C:

List

Fixed data:

The holidays are included in the program and are based on of the corresponding year. Holidays get an "F".

Data:

Birthdays, wedding dates, etc. must have the following format:

Date(8-12 digits) Label (1 digit) Text(19 digits)
Format: t........jyxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

Date:

ttmmyyyy day/month/year
mmttyyyy month/day/year
jjjjtmm Year/day/month The year must always
yjjjmmtt year/month/day 4 digits !!!
tttjjjj lfd.Anniversary/year
jjjjttt year/lfd.anniversary

or

tt?mm?yyyy day/month/year
mm?tt?yyyy month/day/year ? is a filler mark
yjjj?tt?mm year/day/month as . / - spaces
yjjj?mm?tt year/month/day etc.w.
ttt?jjjj lfd.Anniversary/year
yjjj?ttt year/lfd.anniversary

All data is converted internally to the format "ttmmjjj".

If the year is not known, "19 " or "0000" is sufficient. However, no calculation of the number of years is carried out here. (logically!)

Marking:

* for birthday
t for baptism
k for confirmation etc.
o for the wedding day
+ for the date of death
>> for company entry
<< for retirement
F for a public holiday

Dates:

Date(3-12 digits) Text(20 digits)
Format: t........jxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

Date as described under "Data".

In addition, here is the possibility to do without the year. It the calendar year shall be used internally.

The files "Data.DAT" and "Terminexxxx.DAT" can be stored with any belie- Big editors are created and maintained. You can also use data- banks are created. The name of the files is also not an obligation, since ASL Requester ask for the file again before loading and Every possibility is open here. Only the format in the files is logically not changeable.

Joker

source package on Aminet ↗

Jokers

What does Joker do?

Joker does nothing other than make it the old matchpatterns "#?" through Replace a star (*).

I've always found it awkward to put in this MatchPattern command-- and found the idea from the DOSen, a simpler abbreviation to Use, always good.

Well, and what lasts for a long time is finally tormented and then implemented...

How does Joker do this?

In the structures of the DOS there is a so-called rootnode. In this stored (from OS2.0+), which abbreviation is used for pattern matching.

And the programme does nothing other than change this.

Simple, wasn't it?

Therefore also this huge length :) of the program: times lame 600 bytes. And everyone still has it on their WB, right?

Copyright

This is up to me (© 1994 by Jörg), but the program is Freeware, i.e., do what you want with it...

Lots of fun Jörg

Kurzbeschreibung für NewGUI 1.0

source package on Aminet ↗

Short description for NewGUI 1.0

Status 28.02.1998

Content:

  • Foreword (NewGUI <> EasyGUI)
  • Procedures of the NewGUI Module
  • 1 newguiA()
  • 2 guiinitA()
  • 3 guimessage()
  • 4 cleangui()
  • 5 ng setattrsA()
  • TAGs for guiinitA(), newguiA() and ng setattrsA()
  • GUI elements with syntax and description
  • PLUGIN format and procedure description
  • Error messages of procedures
  • Author and addresses
  • 8th Future

1. Foreword:

NewGUI is a proprietary development of THE DARK FRONTIER software development Under the direction of Grundler Mathias. (© 1995-98 THE DARK FRONTIER). NewGUI is NOT a simple copy of EasyGUI (as it is for outsiders) Probably appears at first glance! but an own- constant development. After the appearance of the EasyGUI source (end of 1997) However, some changes were made to a certain compa- tiability to EasyGUI and thus a broader target group speak (a switch or a partial use of NewGUI is therefore Very easy! The source of EasyGUI served only as a template for the change the syntax and the rendering engine (which is adapted to the new syntax) No parts of EasyGUI have been copied or taken over Everything is rewritten and added. There are many similarities, but that is what NewGUI does for many Very interesting, because "old" surface descriptions are very simple It can be used further and you only have to make some minor changes. Although NewGUI has many features and therefore EasyGUI in some disciplines If it is superior, EasyGUI still has some advantages, which are intentionally have not found their way into NewGUI, here are the biggest:

  • NewGUI does NOT have AppWindow support (all programmers I have)
  • know or even questioned needed the AppWindowSupport until
  • Now only in some exceptional situations, others not at all!
  • There is no LITE version of NewGUI (which would also be unnecessary),
  • because then NewGUI and EasyGUI would be in terms of functions yes
  • almost equal and it would only create unnecessary competition!,
  • So the LITE version of EasyGUI is better for smaller programs
  • suitable, while NewGUI many features for larger programs
  • contains (e.g. ARexx port, own screen, more GUI elements ect...)

2. Procedures of the module:

2.1 newguiA()

Is (roughly speaking) a summary of the procedures guiinitA(), guimessage() and cleangui(). Only here (in case the GUI) does not fit on the screen) AUTOMATICally a backfall on the topaz- size 8 font (ROM font). Parameters:

ret:=newguiA(taglist,{dataproc})

The tags of the tag list are listed under (3), {dataproc} is a Pointer on a procedure that receives important data, Here are the transfer parameters:

dataproc(guihandle,screen)

As returncode (ret) 0 is returned if all GUIs are closed (e.g. close gadget of the main GUI) or the number, which was handed over to a gadget instead of a procedure

2.2 guiinitA()

Initialize a Gui and open the associated window, ATTENTION! no actions are handled by the GIU, for which the procedure is guiimessage() responsible!!! This procedure is called:

guihandle:=guiinitA(taglist)

The tags of the tag list are listed under (3). As a return parameter my gets a pointer on the opened guihandle (this must always be indicated at guimessage, except for) you use the MultiGUI handling and add this window to the main gui, then you can (after adding) this variable continue to use (e.g. for the next GUI) or forget!

2.3 guimessage()

Analyses the messages from the GUI and the ARexx port. The window and the surface is refreshed and redrawn if necessary. Syntax:

ret:=guimessage(guihandle)

As a transfer parameter (guihandle) for multiGUI handling only the handle (guihandle) of the main GUI, otherwise (If only 1 window is open ect...) must always be the corresponding guihandle to the window. As a return parameter (ret) you get 0 if the GUI is closed was/should be or a number that can be replaced by a gadget handed over to a procedure.

2.4 cleangui()

If the specified Guihandle closes (in the MultiGUI case), one may DO NOT close with cleangui() but must close ng setattrsA() with the tags NG CLOSEGUI!, only the maingui can / may with cleangui() is closed! Syntax:

cleangui(guihandle,closeall=FALSE)

guihandle is a PTR on the MainGUI or a guihandle of an ON ZELNEN Fensters (No MultiGUI!!!!). closeall indicates in the MultiGUI case that all underguis are also closed They should be!!! (closegui = TRUE therefore means that ALL guis are They should be closed!

2.5 ng setattrsA()

By means of this procedure, most data/tags of the GUIS can can be changed, but also data from the GUI can be fetched. As the most important must ALWAYS be stated the mainguihandle, (Using NG GUI, guihandle,...) will NOT be multiGUIhandling used here is always the respective guihandle of the associated Indicated window! The possible tags are listed under (3) and corresponding Labelled!

TAGS for guiinitA(), newguiA() and ng setattrsA()

NG WINDOWTITLE

A string ('example text') or a PTR to a String to appear in the title line of the window

NG WINDOWLEFT

X-coordinate of the window (relative to the 0-point of the screen)

NG WINDOWTOP

Y-coordinate of the window (relative to the 0-point of the screen)

NG WINDOWWIDTH

  • Main GUI!!!

Syntax...: <1> := Open(<2>,<3>)
<1>: is a so-called Filehandle, that you become the door to a file
can imagine.
<2>: is an e-string that describes an AmigaDOS device. This may include:
the path of a file or the description of a console window
be.
<3>: either OLDFILE or NEWFILE must be entered here.

Function: With this command, files or AmigaDOS window open. For AmigaDOS windows <3> must always be the value NEWFILE have. If this parameter is given for a file, This will be reopened. If this file already exists, The content is lost. The OLDFILE parameter shall be: Only an existing file is opened. Hatch the filehandle <1> the value NIL, the attempt went a file to open obliquely. If this is not the case, read or write data from the file using <1>. Such a file may only be closed by means of Close().

Syntax: Close(<1>)
<1>: is a file handle returned by Open()

Function: This command closes open files. Man Always remember to close open "things". Should If you forget it in this case, this can be a spelling error. Causes that should not be.

Syntax...: <1> := Read(<2>,<3>,<4>)
<1>: is a variable that receives the number of bytes read as a value
<2>: is a file handle as supplied by Open()
<3>: is the address of a memory area, see AllocMem()
<4>: Number of bytes to be read

Function: This procedure reads <4> bytes from the file handle <2> and writes it into the memory area <3>. The number of successfully read bytes is returned as a function value given. Already read bytes can only be read if close the file in between and reopen it again or using the command Seek() nv. Its equivalent for the writing process is Write().

Syntax...: Write(<1>,<2>,<3>)
<1>: is a file handle as supplied by Open()
<2>: is the address of a memory area, see AllocMem()
<3>: Number of bytes to be written

Function: This procedure reads <3> bytes from <2> memory and writes this by means of the file handle <1> into the desired File. The opposite process is Read().

Syntax...: <1> := Input()
<1>: is a file handle as returned by Open()

Function: This function provides you with the current input handle as a function value. If you are writing the following program:

PROC main() -> then a call
WriteF('\d\n',stdin) -> of the program in the CLI
WriteF('\d\n',Input()) -> same number twice
ENDPROC -> issued.

stdin is a file handle of E that handles the current Contains input. Most often, stdin and stdout are identical. See also Output().

Syntax...: <1> := Output()
<1>: is a file handle as returned by Open()

Function: This function provides you with the current output handle as a function value. It works just like the Input() function, only for the output handle. It corresponds to the e-variable stdout.

Syntax...: <1> := SetComment(<2>,<3>)
<1>: is a variable that receives the value TRUE or FALSE
<2>: is a string containing a full path
<3>: is any character string

Function: The file <2> receives the comment <3>. FALSE, no comment could be attached. With TRUE Everything was normal.

Syntax...: <1> := SetProtection(<2>,<3>)
<1>: is a variable that receives the value TRUE or FALSE
<2>: is a string containing a full path
<3>: is an 8-bit mask for the protection bits

Function: This command corresponds to the DOS command "Protect". If this command is successful at <2>, then <1> has the value TRUE, Otherwise, false. AmigaDOS currently has 8 protection bits:

| Title | On | Off | Function
Bit 0 | deletable d | 0 | 1 | file is erasable
Bit 1 | executable e | 0 | 1 | File is executable
Bit 2 | writable w | 0 | 1 | File is writable
Bit 3 | readable r | 0 | 1 | File is readable
Bit 4 | archived a | 1 | 0 | File is an archive
Bit 5 | pure p | 1 | 0 | File contains resident code
Bit 6 | script s | 1 | 0 | File is a batch file
Bit 7 | ?????? h | 1 | 0 | ???????????

If the file is executable and contains resident code, the mask looks as follows: %00101101.

Introduction

MMV stands for MusicModuleAdministration. The name does not like much sound pretty, but I couldn't think of a better one, and I liked it. The shortcut is even better for me. In addition, the name describes exactly that, What MMV does. It is a special file management for sound modules of all kinds. If If you have hundreds of megabytes of modules, you'll end up in chaos. no longer knows where a particular module is and/or you have several Modules double. When this problem occurred to me (intermediately) During the time it is acute I decided to solve it, There had to be an administration. At the beginning of 1994 I started my idea- sam and with time the program became better and better and more efficient. At the beginning of 1996 I started it completely new with Amiga-E. write (MaxonPascal just did not bring it anymore).

System requirements

  • at least OS2.04 (V37), but 3.0 is recommended because some radio
  • tionen can only be used under this version
  • a 68000 is enough, but better 68020
  • 512KB Ram is sufficient for start-up, but for large amounts of data
  • no longer guaranteed (the more ram the better)
  • HiRes screen and proportional system fonts are recommended
  • The following libraries are absolutely necessary:
  • reqtools.library V38 (attached)
  • gadtools.library (actually everyone should have)
  • rexxsys.library (should have everyone too)
  • CrM.library or its demo version (included), otherwise not with
  • packed data files can be worked
  • protracker.library (attached) so that you can use ProTracker modules
  • can be played
  • Eagleplayer1.54 is recommended because data recording is
  • Much simpler is

Installation

You copy all libraries from the Libs folder from the MMV into its 'LIBS:' directory, unless you already have it. Finished. Double click on the icon and you can go.

Use

The operation of MMV is actually quite simple, the most self- Explanatory notes. The functions in detail:

GADGETS:

CLOSEWINDOW - Ends the program immediately (!). END - Finishes the program properly in any situation. Load - A file requester appears with which you can load a Select the file. MMV recognizes whether the file is MMV data. Event. existing data will be processed after previous security request deleted. SAFETY - The data is displayed under the name visible in the screenbar stored. GRAFIK - The number of different lengths of each module will be graphically illustrated. LONG - The size of all modules are added and output. PRESSURE - This allows the individual data to be printed. First you have the choice for a tabular expression (should always be chosen for larger amounts of data) and a 'normal' pressure (needs more space on paper), But it is more complete. Then you have the choice of only the current data set wants to print all data or only a specific area. EXTEND - Creates a new (and empty) record. If you have created an empty data set, you can put your data into the Enter string and integer gadgets. Insert a new data set into an existing one Insert data field (extend only) For this you choose with the Cursorgadgets the corresponding Stop. Delete - here the current data set or the entire data- field is deleted. If you only want to delete certain but larger areas, save delete the other sub-areas ('save from to..') everything and loads the individual parts again one after the other Then there is (the charge). Comparison - Here the length of the individual modules is included Compared and duplicate lengths are output. Search - A requester appears in which you select what you are looking for To be (name or length). Sort - Here you can add your data by name or length Increasingly sort.

CURSORGADGETS:

> - A data set further forward.
>> - Ten data sets further forward.
>>> - One hundred records further forward.
>| - Last data set.
|< - First data set.
<<< - One hundred records back.
<< - Ten records back.
< - A record back.

MENUS - Project:

About - An information requester appears. Loading - see corresponding gadget Charges - Works as described under 'charges', only the event. existing data not deleted, but the new Loaded data is simply attached to the back. SAFE - see corresponding gadget SAFE THANS - A file requester appears, with which you can distribute your data can store. SAFE FROM TOIS - Two requesters appear in which you can see the values from where to where to be stored. Otherwise, as described in gadget 'SAFE'. PACKAGE SAFE THANS - All existing data is stored with the help of CrM.library and can then be stored. For larger amounts of data, this may take some time, This is the packing rate and the unpacking rate. Speed enormous. ICONISING - MMV iconizes into an AppIcon. DELETE FILE - A file quester appears with which you can use any file can be deleted. END - Terminates the program after previous security request.

MENU - Special:

EXTERNAL COMPATIBILITY - A file requester appears with which an external file can be compared with the internal data (according to the module length). Possibly doubling... The modules are issued. PALETTE - A color palette for changing the screen colors appears. TASKPRIORITITY - The priority of the program can be set. Zero for normal work, +5 for a preference of MMV (so that, for example, the sorting time does not run out if a ray tracer is working in the background) and -5 if Other programs are more important. Other values in the range From -15 to +15 are also possible. WB OPEN/CLOSE - Try to open or close the workbench screen It depends on what is present. DATA SURVEILLANCE - Activated, it changes the next menu function. Then a new data set is created, then the Moduleinfo read out and finally tries to bene ARexx command. READ EAGLEPLAYER - The module info from said Player readable (tested with EP version 1.54d). COLDREBOOT - This allows the computer to receive a security request duly resettled.

Menu - Music:

Charges a ProTracker module and plays it. Removes the module from memory. Play - Plays the module. Stop - Stop playing. GAME FROM PATH - Try to load the file in the 'Path' string gadget and play.

Menu - ARexx:

OBJECTIVE PORT CHANGE - Requester to enter the port and command name appear. AREXX-KOMMANDO - Attempting a Rexx-Msg to the selected port with the corresponding command string. EXPORT SCRIPT - A file quester appears with which one can Selects any Arexx script that then executes will. But this requires the file 'rx', which either in the folder 'C:', 'Rexx:' or 'SYS:Rexxc' must be.

Error

I am not aware of any mistakes, but the devil may be stuck. Somewhere in the detail. Of course, I tried hard to get all the error source- len to be eliminated. Also, I have the program for a time of 2 Let friends test, and of course I have it throughout Development phase tested itself. Also I have MMV with Enforcer over- Checked, hits did not occur.

Test configurations

MMV was tested for running ability on the following computers:

A1200/030/50 2MB chip, 16MB Fast (Blizzard1230-III), Overdrive CD, 1.2GB HD
A1200/030/50 2MB chip, 8MB Fast (Blizzard1230-IV), OverDrive CD, 400MB HD
A1200/030/28 2MB chip, 4MB Fast (M-TEC turbo card), 250MB HD
A1200/020/14 2MB chip, 40MB HD
A500 with Kick2.04, 1MB Chip 1.8MB Fast
A600 with kick2.04, 2MB chip, 60MB HD

But it should actually run on all other Amigas, which meet the system requirements.

MMV has a built-in ARexx port with which it can be connected via ARexx commands partially remotely controlled. In this version there are only very few commands sent to the ARexx port of MMV ("MMV REXX") can be. On the other hand, MMV can also use ARexx for other programs, such as Eagleplayer remote control. Further information on this in the chapter Use under The menu 'ARexx'. Attention: If you want to work with ARexx, the program must always 'RexxMast' (SYS:System/RexxMast), Otherwise nothing will work. It is best to put it in the WBStartup folder.

Introduction

Maybe someone knows the "WB voter" I came across sometime am. You could take the dialing of phone numbers from the compi leave. Idea good, execution, well, not so great. Written in Basic, Not font sensitive... The MUI voter should provide a remedy. He is, no one can think of it, a MUI application and was developed with the awesome AmigaE of Wouter van Oortmerssen programmed. Thus, the MUI voter also has all the Great benefits of MUI. (fontsensitive, self-configurable...)

You need...

  • hmm, an Amiga (of course only from OS 2.0 WARP)
  • MUI 2.3 or better
  • a modem (VM 2400 does it too)

Installation

Draw the MUI voter and icon into a suitable directory, MUI must If necessary, be installed beforehand in accordance with the MUI documentation. Finished.

Use

When called, the MUI voter reads the file ENV:MUI/Waehler.data in which a list of names with the associated telephone numbers is stored. (This is) File does not exist at the first launch of the MUI voter, of course, but what It is not, can still be... After that, it also appears that Main window.

The main window is divided into three sub-windows (name list, entry), Modem actions). With the button "New" under the name list, a a new entry in the name list is made. This can be done in the sub-window "Entry" the name and associated telephone number are provided. With the "Accept" button or the "Return" button, this entry is entered into the Name list adopted. With the button "Edit" under the name list, a Entry can be changed, with "Delete" an entry can be deleted. With one simple mouse click on an entry this will be with the matching Phone number displayed in the "Entry" sub-window, a double click on a Entry is sufficient to have the corresponding telephone number dialed. Choosing can be used either with the selection type ATDP (pulse selection) or ATDT (multi-frequency selection) are made. The choice between the two procedures is made with the Switch "Art" under "Modem actions". Here you can also find a simply clicked, i.e. select "active" entry of the name list from the modem leave ("select", same effect as double click on entry) or the modem hang up ("hang up"). In the pulldown menu you can enter the debug mode which outputs all data sent via the serial.device in CON:. Of course, the delays are not displayed, but executed beforehand. In addition, you can go to the Preferences and "About" Give some information about the program.

Preferences

The Preferences window allows settings for data exchange with Change the modem.

Usually the serial.device is used, owner of a MultifaceCard but use the duart.deivce and can then use it here Enter. Likewise with the unit which with 0 already has the correct value for Ordinary user.

In addition, the settings for the serial.device or Others responsible for direct contact with the modem. Since only very simple and short data are transmitted to the modem, these values are not relevant, as this is not a large speed advantage. Maybe some users with their Settings problems and can change this.

Initstring and HangUpstring have been added to give everyone the opportunity to set the optimal call for his modem. to my ears It has come that some had problems with the set delay, This should no longer be the case. The predefined settings It works with a Zyxel U-1496E.

With the baudbandit.device, the MUI voter does not work.

  • Initstring,HangUpstring

NewDir is an improved Dir command, as it is already on the work- Bench exists. He masters 1-3 column output, automatic variety- Ren, create command sequences (such as List) and stop the output a certain number of lines. NewDir can call the ASL requester and thus also for a "RequestFile/RequestYour" function "abused"- den. The most comprehensive function is to display the types of listed files. It is also possible to define your own file types. NewDir is reentrant and can thus be copied into RAM with the command Resident so that it does not have to be reloaded at every call.

In the unregistered version, some functions are blocked. If: If you also want to use them, you should register. The unre- However, you may use the current version without restriction. It is up to you completely free whether you pay the share fee.

NewDir was written with AmigaE 2.1b (hence the - unnecessary - Open some libraries) and is available from OS 2.04 (V37) on all Amiga min. 512 kB of RAM running.

In the current version of NewDir, I am only aware of one error:

  • NewDir should never call with the parameter -i several times at the same time-
  • It will cause a crash under warranty. This error
  • but seems to be with the whatis.library, which gives me a fix
  • The same is impossible.

NewDir’s call is as follows:

NewDir [<directory>] [-r] [-c <columns>] [-nf] [-nd] [-f] [-na] [-h]
[-p <lines>] [-t <directory>] [-a] [-rf] [-pt <pattern>] [-s]
[-i] [-ls] [-ti <title>] [-pg <text>] [-ng <text>] [-si]
[-lf <Format string>]

If NewDir is called with the parameter "HELP", a short-term View over all parameters. For the registered version, additional The user's name and registration number are still displayed.

ATTENTION: for the unregistered version, the output redirection from the Shell into a file (e.g. "NewDir >RAM:Script") is not possible.

<Directory> specifies which directory should be displayed. If not specified, the current directory is displayed. Serves for use- of -a, -rf or -s also for setting the default directory.

-r indicates that the directory is recursive (with subdirectories) to be displayed. No effect at -rf and -s.

-c serves to set the number of columns (1-3). Preset: 2. None Action at -rf, -s, -i and -ls.

-nf turns off the output of the files.

-nd turns off the output of subdirectories. No effect on -rf and -s.

-f turns on the full path for each file. No effect on -rf and -s.

-na turns off the ANSI representation. No effect at -rf and -s.

-h turns on the "Directory of ...": header. Especially Useful for -r. No effect at -rf and -s.

-p enforces a "Press <Return>" after a certain number of lines To continue. No effect at -rf and -s.

-t sets the destination directory for -d. No effect at -rf and -s.

-a calls the ASL requester. Requires the asl.library (minor version) 37). -a depends on -nf. If you prefer the more comfortable file re- quester of reqtools.library, you should use the program RTPatch by Nico François. It changes the asl.library so that This calls the reqtools.library.

-rf activates the RequestFile/RequestDir function. Leave it a file or select a directory (depending on -nf), which then goes to StdOut is issued. -rf automatically activates -a.

This parameter is locked in the unregistered version.

-pt sets the default pattern for -rf, -s and -a. -a.

-s specifies use of the "save" mode, in which only other Colors are used. Automatically activates -rf and -a.

-i turns on the display of file types. For this function, the whatis.library (minimum version 3) and optionally the file »FileTypes« in the Drawing S: Needed. By default, the deep scan is used.

This parameter is locked in the unregistered version.

-ls activates Light Scan. Automatically activates -i.

-ti activates a title other than "NewDir file requester" for the ASL requester. No effect on all parameters except -a, -rf, -s, -pt, -pg and -ng. Activates automatically -a.

-pg activates text other than "Okay" for the positive gadget of the ASL requesters. No effect on all parameters except -a, -rf, -s, -pt and -ng. Activates automatically -a.

-ng activates text other than "Cancel" for the negative gadget of the ASL requesters. No effect on all parameters except -a, -rf, -s, -pt and -pg. Activates automatically -a.

-si activates the output of the total size of all listed files.

-lf indicates which command is connected to the displayed files No effect on -rf and -s. This parameter must be the last are given because everything after "-lf" as a single argument for -lf It is seen (even if spaces do not require quotes). This is However, it is favorable insofar as it can also be used when the command is to be executed. They can use signs. The following format characters can be used den:

%s normal filename (full path)
%f as %s, but without extension (“.txt” or similar)
%r is like %f, but the directory that normally appears
is replaced by the directory at -t (if -t is not entered)
ben, the source directory is used
%>\ effect the same as the shell output redirects (have to)
%>> }- but be used so that the shell does not think that it is
%< / means, and plays crazy

Here are some examples:

Suppose you want all the instructions you have in the DOK directory: have stored, print. So you would use the Type command. But why call every single file with type if you automatically create a command dot and then execute it Can it be executed? So you give the following command in a shell one:

NewDir DOK: -nd -lf Type "%s" to PRT:

or

NewDir DOK: -nd -lf Type %>PRT: "%s"

Now the order sequence appears in the shell. To put them in a file to get that can be executed with Execute, you need to Gabe diversion:

NewDir >RAM:Command file DOK: -nd -lf Type %>PRT: "%s"

Now to run the file, enter this:

Execute RAM: command file

2. To compile all AmigaE source codes (also in subdirectories) If you are in the ESource: directory, you can: Use lines:

NewDir >RAM:Instruction file ESource: -r -nd -lf EC "%f"
Execute RAM: command file

This parameter is locked in the unregistered version.

First up front: if you define file types that are not yet in of the file "FileTypes", separate them from the already visible (“#” introduces comment). Please send them then the file type and some example files to my address.

Now a file type example (it is recommended to use all "commands" in capital) staben, as this serves among other things for better readability:

# File type example:
TYPE "Instructions" # This defines a new type. The name may:
# max. 9 characters long.

SUBTYPE "Text" # Optional: the file MUST be of type "Text",
# otherwise it cannot be a “guide”.

Insert "Script" # Optional: the type "Instructions" is displayed in the
# Type list inserted after “Script”. These
# List is not ordered alphabetically. The
# Result can be e.g. in BrowserII with »Sort/by«
#file type are considered. This option
# you can safely omit for NewDir.

ICONNAME "def instruction" # Optional: this is the name of the default icon
# for files of type “Instructions”. This name
# should always be "def <type name>". These
# Option is not (yet) in NewDir either
# Used.

# Now comes the actual type definition. If any of the conditions are
# ung does not apply, the corresponding file does not correspond to this type
# ordered (the only exception is OPTNAMEPATTERN).

NAMEPATTERN "#?.dok" # Optional: the name must be of this pattern
Fill #. Cannot be combined with OPTNAMEPAT-
# TERN are used.

OPTNAMEPATTERN "#?.dok" #Optional: like NAMEPATTERN, but it is a
# Deep scan, this pattern does not have to fit.

# Now the deep scan definition begins. Numbers can be decimal, hexade-
#cimal (with a “$” at the beginning) or binary (with a “%” at the beginning)
# are given. Strings must be included in "". One of the
# tei is currently only examined for the first 484 bytes. All follow--
# the options are optional and are considered applicable during a light scan
# End viewed.

# Now the options:

# COMPAREBYTE <Offset> <string>

COMPAREBYTE 12 $AFFE # Test for string from offset 12
#$AFFE.

COMPAREBYTE $23 "Hello" # Test from offset $23 (decimal 35) on the
# String "Hello".

# SEARCHBYTE <string>

SEARCHBYTE "Amiga" # Look for the string "Amiga".

SEARCHBYTE $AFFE # Look for the string $AFFE.

# SEARCHPATTERN [CASE] <Pattern> # CASE causes that between large
# and lowercase letters distinguished
# becomes.

SEARCHPATTERN CASE "ST-??:" # Looking for a string that goes into the
# Pattern »ST-??:« fits and observes
# Capital/Little Letter.

# MATCHPATTERN [CASE] <Offset> <Pattern>

MATCHPATTERN 12 "ST-??:" # Determines whether there is a point at offset 12
# chenfollow is written in the pattern
"Sh-??:" fits.

ENDTYPE # Displays the end of the type definition.

Imagine hanging on the file names of your ILBM files The ending ".ilbm". Then in a light scan all their ILBM files would be recognized. ILBM files can also be detected internally via deep scan will become. So if you specify "NAMEPATTERN" "#?.ilbm" all ILBM-Da- teien that do not end with .ilbm (some people use .iff) or ".pic", not recognized. But if you instead “OPTNAMEPATT” "#?.ilbm", this is ignored by the deep scan and ILBM files are recognized. Thus, in Light-Scan (by OPT-) NAMEPATTERN) AND ALL ILBM files detected during deep scan.

This example lags, of course, since the whatis.library is already ILBM-Da- teien recognizes, even without having to load a “FileTypes” file.

Basically, there are two different scan types: light and deep scan. Light scanning recognizes the type of a file by its name. The deep- Scan, on the other hand, currently reads the first 484 bytes of a file and evaluates And then they leave. This results in a higher and more accurate recognition rate. provided. By reading in the deep scan, however, it is time-intense. siver.

What is NewGUI?

NewGUI is a module for the programming language >Amiga E< which It should make it easier for the programmer to provide an interface for Writing the program. NewGUI offers some skills and additions (e.g. drag 'N' drop, ARexx port, online help...) which make the surface very high quality, but the effort Keep it minimal for creation. NewGUI was created in early 1995, but the first 4-5 versions not exactly acceptable (of appearance, ect..., but gradually grew from this Idea of a mature GUI engine. At the end of 1997, the source- Code for EasyGUI was published I used this (NOT COOPERATE!) to make my GUI engine compatible with Easygui Syntax Compatible. The plugin interface of NewGUI was also adapted, but the benefits of NewGUI were (Drag 'N' Drop...). A few claim that NewGUI is simply a cheap Copy of EasyGUI, but it has NOT become part of EasyGUI Sources copied, this served only as a template and as a lookup- work for suggestions - NewGUI is therefore not a copy, and everything Other than cheap! I have been asked why I do not publish the source of NewGUI to prove this, but that is not my intention, otherwise it would similar to EasyGUI (and D**M) and go at once There are many variations, and this leads to a Total chaos...

What distinguishes NewGUI from other surface generators?

Unlike most other surface generators (e.g. MUI, Triton, BGUI...) NewGUI is not an External Library or external classes, this can be used both as pre- and See it as a disadvantage. In any case, it is clear that NewGUI It is not as overloaded as MUI and others. not every application needs APP icon support, commoditie- Properties ect... also most MUI elements are no real intuition gadgets (proof: there are in AmiNet) a program, I think it's called "ShowGadgets", which all Intuition gadgets (and BOOPSI classes) of a window show can - but only the sliders of MUI are shown as such! and bypass intuition partially (it will only be the MOUSEMOVE) and uses BUTTONUP/BUTTONDOWN messages of the mouse, no Intuition button message! This can slow down of the system and (possibly) to incompatibilities with later Operating system versions are coming (NewGUI uses GadTools-) Gadgets, so benefits from every further development of GadTool.library!! But it is in the hands of the programmers which engine He wants to use it because the surface generator which Everything can be done 100% like the programmer and the user wants is not yet developed! (This should be) be the task of the operating system programmers and not of a third-party provider!

PTR on an already opened screen, this is then Used for windows, but NOT at termination Closed!

Only useful with MultiWindow Support! If this day is TRUE, then this window will immediately open at the beginning, otherwise it is initialized, but closed, it must then be opened with NG OPENGUI!

PTR on a Textattr, (Font must be open!), this Font will then be used for THIS window!

Name of the font to be used (this is opened if necessary!) Only useful in conjunction with NG FONT SIZE! ATTENTION! In conjunction with the module ng guitask.m, which running the surface in a separate task caused the use of this tag (AND NG FONT SIZE) hangers!

NG FONT SIZE

What is NewGUI?

NewGUI is a module for the programming language >Amiga E< which It should make it easier for the programmer to provide an interface for Writing the program. NewGUI offers some skills and additions (e.g. drag 'N' drop, ARexx port, online help...) which make the surface very high quality, but the effort Keep it minimal for creation. NewGUI was created in early 1995, but the first 4-5 versions not exactly acceptable (of appearance, ect..., but gradually grew from this Idea of a mature GUI engine. At the end of 1997, the source- Code for EasyGUI was published I used this (NOT COOPERATE!) to make my GUI engine compatible with Easygui Syntax Compatible. The plugin interface of NewGUI was also adapted, but the benefits of NewGUI were (Drag 'N' Drop...). A few claim that NewGUI is simply a cheap Copy of EasyGUI, but it has NOT become part of EasyGUI Sources copied, this served only as a template and as a lookup- work for suggestions - NewGUI is therefore not a copy, and everything Other than cheap! I have been asked why I do not publish the source of NewGUI to prove this, but that is not my intention, otherwise it would similar to EasyGUI (and D**M) and go at once There are many variations, and this leads to a Total chaos...

What distinguishes NewGUI from other surface generators?

Unlike most other surface generators (e.g. MUI, Triton, BGUI...) NewGUI is not an External Library or external classes, this can be used both as pre- and See it as a disadvantage. In any case, it is clear that NewGUI It is not as overloaded as MUI and others. not every application needs APP icon support, commoditie- Properties ect... also most MUI elements are no real intuition gadgets (proof: there are in AmiNet) a program, I think it's called "ShowGadgets", which all Intuition gadgets (and BOOPSI classes) of a window show can - but only the sliders of MUI are shown as such! and bypass intuition partially (it will only be the MOUSEMOVE) and uses BUTTONUP/BUTTONDOWN messages of the mouse, no Intuition button message! This can slow down of the system and (possibly) to incompatibilities with later Operating system versions are coming (NewGUI uses GadTools-) Gadgets, so benefits from every further development of GadTool.library!! But it is in the hands of the programmers which engine He wants to use it because the surface generator which Everything can be done 100% like the programmer and the user wants is not yet developed! (This should be) be the task of the operating system programmers and not of a third-party provider!

PAGE

source package on Aminet ↗

PAGE

I get a question again and again from people who actively exchange with me EMAILS: "Where can I get the EPD's from?". Previous answer: "From Daniel or Gregor by post.".

But that was not what many wanted. Rather, They wanted to get the EPD's sent by EMAIL. and This has not been possible so far...

So far! That is the end of the matter. And that is why there is PAGE.

What does PAGE mean?

PAGE means

Put put and Get EPD.

PUT should first tell you that whoever wants something, I want to give something too! Namely YOUR programs, sources, tips, etc. to E.

But please no programs from the network or from the AmiNet. To the We have access ourselves. Because we want to have your programs.

And when you give something, you get something... In this case, an EPD of your choice for each program/project, that you have created.

Where do I send the programs via EMAIL?

To my EMAIL address, which is:

Joerg.Wach@….

And in the SUBJECT or subject you should "PAGE" as well as the EPD that you Wishing to show it (if not in a second EMAIL) with a small, nice letter additionally mentioned. The EPD's are sent as "LZX" file.

Examples:

1) User xyz sends me a program and wants the EPD39:

Subject: PAGE 39

2) User xyz sends me a program disk and wants the EPD1 as a DMS file:

Subject: PAGE 1

Hard, isn't it? :

How do I know what the individual EPDs contain?

Also zero problem. Just send an EMAIL with the subject or the Subject

Subject: PAGE CONTENT.

The table of contents then goes back to the sender.

What do I do if I have no programs?

For this, there is, as before, the order with Daniel or Gregor.

What is PAGE?

The EPD series is (to this day) the only floppy series, which exists for the e-compiler.

The series has developed very positively in the past 2 years, And that should remain so!

However, many programmers shy away from their sending programs by normal post or over and above Get EPDs.

On the other hand, the EPD lives from e-programs that are produced by others programmers are provided. So it should be a allowing the EPD to become larger and, on the other hand, the users, who have INTERNET access, can get their EPD's faster.

And therefore PAGE.

PAGE is © 1996 by Jörg Wach.

Comments and suggestions are very welcome.

Another comment from me: since the whole thing is still in the test stage It may happen that there are problems. Please Do not despair, but send an EMAIL to me.

If for some reason PAGE no longer works, I share it with you.

Byte says Jörg

ParsePattern

from Gregor Goldbach

Programme description and status

ParsePattern demonstrates the use of the ParsePattern() routines and MacthPattern() of dos.library from OS 2.04. There are various signs. chains are tested for matching with patterns and the results are output.

ParsePattern is public domain, do what you want with it. It shall: there is no guarantee that the information is correct or are complete, nor that the program is error-free. Use on their own danger.

Description of the ParsePattern() and MatchPattern() routines

ParsePattern() converts a pattern string into an internal format, the MatchPattern() is passed and expects three parameters: Wildcard- string address, buffer address and buffer length. Return value is -1, if an error occurred, for example, if the buffer was too small.

The wildcard string contains the mentioned pattern string which contains the can contain the same wild cards that are also used in the shell, For example, '#?', '~', etc.

After termination of the function, the buffer becomes the converted character- Chain included. This will be used by MatchPattern().

The buffer length can indicate the extent to which the buffer to be used.

MatchPattern() compares a string with that of ParsePattern() patterns developed. If successful, 1 is returned. The string, whose address is passed as a second argument, but may not Wildcards included.

Shell Tools Collection

by Andreas Rehm

©1994-95

Status: GiftWare - no liability on my part and no cost for their part.

General:

The Shell Tools collection contains several different programs. All should be documented here and sufficiently pressed. This collection was created because it is hardly suitable for programs of 1000 bytes. It is worthwhile to create an archive. So it's easier and takes less time. I assume no liability for the software contained here. Error are fixed after bug reports, if possible.

Please read the texts in the SOFTINFO program. Only the window is valid for this collection at the moment programming language. Updates and general are regulated differently.

Some programs are able to use ReqTools or Dosrequester.

ReqTools are © Copyright by Nico François ©1992-1994

Programme list and descriptions:

DEFPUBSCRWB V1.1
DelTrash V1.13
FReset V1.0
MouseCheck V1.001
MouseXY V1.01
Reset.cli V1.2
Reset V1.11
Res V1.05
ShellStarter V1.02
Wipe V1.04

DEFPUBSCRWB:

This program makes the Workbench screen again as a public screen DEFAULT. This means that all windows, as well as requesters etc. are back on the Workbench is opened. So the program basically serves to redirect everyone. Put the window back on the DEFAULT, i.e. on the workbench.

DelTrash:

DelTrash is a small program that empties the trash can of the workbench. It requires the Delete command of the Workbench.

This program deletes all (!!!) files present in the >SYS:Trashcan<! So don't throw anything important into the trashcan. You can only do it on the SYS: Trashcan, so on the trash can of the currently active Workbench.

You can simply use the program in the Cli. This is done by Enter >DelTrash< in an active shell or menu >Enter command...< (Project Menu of the Wokbench) But you can also use it in the >S:User-Startup<, for which it was Written simply by:

Path:DelTrash

inserts. Where you insert the command does not matter. Path: is the directory, in You can find DelTrash. (Can also be used on another partition of a hard disk.

FReset:

FReset is a very small program. If you start it by CLI/Shell, then it waits 2 seconds and then performs a reset.

MouseCheck:

MouseCheck is a fairly simple program but it can be very useful can. It checks whether the left/right/center or the left and right Mouse button is pressed. Depending on the status of the mouse, LB, RB, LB+RB or MB is issued.

LB = left mouse button MB = middle mouse button
RB = right mouse button LB+RB = left and right mouse button

You can only use this program in scripts. In another way, It makes no sense! Not to leave the inexperienced among you. leave here an example of using MouseCheck:

/* Simple example script */

MouseCheck >ENV:Result ; The result is the variable
if $result eq "LB"
echo "Left button pressed "
endif
unsetenv >NIL: result ; Delete variable result

This Scipt runs MouseCheck. Then the system gets the output of the program and evaluates them as Vaiable. Then the script makes a Comparison (if ...) and gives the respective result with a suitable variable. In this case, the left button is pressed while the script was started, the variable set to "LB" and the if loop leads An echo. In the output window appears >Left button pressed<.

In this archive there is also an example script that you can view Should! It should work properly and can be adopted as such. However, you should let your own functions be performed.

MouseXY:

MouseXY is a program that opens a small window, and in this the Mouse coordinates. It is a bit computationally intensive, since it is about 8 to 25% can swallow computing power. It is done by simultaneously pressing the left and right mouse button finished, so beware if you do not finish it yet Will!

Res:

Res is a program that extends into the Workbench menu tools is integrated. When you start it, it asks if you keep it in memory. will. If so, in the aid menu the entry "" Reset " remains. This entry leads to the reset shortly after activation. It is a pause programmed in so that the read access to your medium is not yet It is underway. The program warns through a DisplayBeep() before the reset executed. However, an abort is no longer possible!

Reset:

Reset is a program that uses a requester to ask if there is a reset shall be carried out. If this is desired, a reset will occur after a break. carried out.

Reset.cli:

Reset is a CLI/Shell command that performs a reset after a query.

ShellStarter:

The shell starter is a simple program that can be used in the Tools Menu of Workbench hung in. When it starts, it asks if it should start. When you start it leaves, then in the tool menu you can find the entry => shell <=. When activated, the program opens a new shell and asks, whether it should be removed or remain resident.

Wipe:

Wipe is a deletion program that fills files with zeros, the file length Change it and then delete it. This leaves nothing of the file. So it's A program that actually terminates files! With Disksalv, deleted files can no longer be saved. You can delete confidential files.

[1m] The call for Wipe is:[22m]

Wipe arg1 arg2 ...argx

argx for any number of arguments (files)

[1mVersions:[22m]

V1.00 - First version that only did its service up to 25000 bytes
V1.01 - Texts provided with color
- Program extended to delete files over 25000 bytes
- Display the progress in the file to be deleted in percent and
Byte done / Byte to to
- Delete function for file not filled with zeros (as safe as
before, so does not bring much
- unfortunately somewhat slow, since each byte is written individually into the file
It will be what I have hopefully fixed in a next version.
- Call can now contain many files => The call is:
Wipe arg1 arg2 arg 3 arg4 ... arg10 ... argx
- Icons are also deleted (not terminated)
- New structure, completely rewritten
- Abort is always possible, but if something is terminated, wait
the program until the end of the destruction of the file, until it cancels
V1.01 - The first officially released version of Wipe
- The program has been totally reprogrammed and changed
- Display of the file length replaced at the start of the destruction process
Percentage and Byte done / Byte to do Display
- Only destruction of the files, since now functional
- Now proper binary zero characters are used so that really
Nothing remains
- Much faster than V1.00 and V1.01ß, since now each 30,000 bytes with
binary zeros are filled, and then the rest
--> Speed gain: more than 100 times faster (>100,000%)
V1.02 - Comments added
- Names that are longer than 80 characters from this version until
360 characters still displayed correctly
Useless definition removed
V1.03 - Unnecessary rename removed
- Buffer with binary 00000000 removed and by %0000000000 in the call
Replaced for Write().
V1.04 - Rename function reinstated, because without it the file length is not
shall be brought to zero:
- old version of the overwrite buffer reinstated, since the new
had not worked

Short: Some Modules/Sources (with Executables) for AmigaE and for EasyGUI

source package on Aminet ↗

Short: Some Modules/Sources (with Executables) for AmigaE and for EasyGUI
Author: turrican@… (Mathias Grundler)
Uploader: turrican@…
Version: 1.4
Type: dev/e
Replaces: Egui-Tools.lha

ENGLISH:

This is a package of some useful Sources and Modules for AmigaE. There are some for EasyGUI, which made it very flexbile and very better than before (Plugin`s and Flexible-GUI`s-Design...), and there are some for handling requesters easier (ReqTools+ASL for example Screenmode-Requesters, Filerquesters aso...

New in 1.3: (not released in AmiNet!)

Minor bug fixes... now completly Enforcer-HIT-Free and 100% Stable!! - Fixed for use with EasyGUI 3.3a (no crashes, no gfx-failures!) - added editor-class, now its easy to create your own editor! (show to the source!) Image plugin completly rewritten (now totally based on Intui-) gadgets! only 2 kb big module and this module contains only 1 KB code!!! Now its much easier to use the plugin!

New in 1.4:

Added NewMem (No longer Errors or Software Failure because of Wrong assigned or wrong freed memory! (Now its easy to find meme leaks!)

Germany:

This is a collection of nutshell source texts and modules for Amiga-E. There are e.g. modules/sources for EasyGUI, which make EasyGUI more flexible and powerful (plugins) and an example of how to design flexible GUI`s..., also Modules are included to make Requester (ReqTools or ASL) better and easier to integrate (e.g. screenmode requester) and Filerequester...

New in 1.3: (Not released in AmiNet!)

- Bigger bug fixes... now there are NO more Enforcer hits and No other bugs (according to Sushi ect...) - All plugins for EasyGUI 3.3a revised (no crashes) More, no graphic errors! - Added editor class (now it's easy to see its Its own editor for programming! See the source! - Image plugin completely rewritten... it is now 100% based on intuition gadgets and is only 2 kb tall! In which The module contains only 800 bytes of code! The programming has now been made even easier and the memory consumption is just at the size of the loaded Liked icons!!

New in 1.4:

- NewMem added (never more crashes due to incorrect memory-) Request or false memory release! Now it's easy to find memory leaks and crashes. avoid, now also finally can NO memory of their pro- grams more are lost (Each unreleased memory) Will be released at the end of the program!

ShowSlides 2.0 - © 20-Jan-1994 by Maik Schreiber

source package on Aminet ↗

ShowSlides 2.0 - © 20-Jan-1994 by Maik Schreiber

  • Introduction

  • Guarantee provisions (English)

ShowSlides is a program that allows you to make your own slides. Putting together the show. It offers an easy-to-use interface, on which all gadgets are also addressable by keyboard shortcut. ShowSlides can open its windows on any PublicScreen. The total Surface is localized and can therefore be adapted to any language.

With the program ShowSlidesPlayer you play your script files. The invited pictures are not - as with many other pro- grams - just fade in and out again, but are combined with Several wipe effects on the screen.

ShowSlides starts with a simple double click on the icon. You can also enter the program name into a shell.

The ShowSlidesPlayer is started by calling a script Indicate the file:

Shell : ShowSlidesPlayer <Script file>

A slideshow with ShowSlidesPlayer can be done by pressing the left or The right mouse button is aborted.

Each line of a script consists of the following 15 parameters, which are What effect and how it should be executed. The simple- For the sake of clarity, letters are given in brackets behind the parameters. These letters also serve in the user interface of ShowSlides as Keyboard abbreviations.

Effect (a) Width (f) Type (k)
x1 (b) Height (g) Colour (l)
y1 (c) Parameter1 (h) Delay (m)
x2 (d) Parameter2 (i) VBI (n)
y2 (e) Parameter3 (j) Pause (o)

The following parameters are required for each effect:

a: indicates the number of the effect,
b: indicates the left edge of the effect area on the source screen
(only if "k" > 0; otherwise 0),
c: indicates the upper edge of the effect area on the source screen
(only if "k" > 0; otherwise 0),
d: indicates the left edge of the effect area on the target screen,
e: indicates the upper edge of the effect area on the target screen,
f: indicates the width of the effect range,
g: indicates the height of the effect range,
k: indicates the effect type:
0: Effect area is filled with color (see "l"),
1: Target screen is deleted, effect area of the source screen
is copied to effect area of the target screen (e.g. for nor-
inviting and displaying an image,
2: like 1, but without deleting the target screen (e.g., to be removed from a
already displayed image delete an area or an
over-fading the altered part of the image,
l: indicates the color with which the effect area on the target screen
is filled (only if "k" = 0; otherwise 0),
m: indicates how much the execution of an effect should be delayed
(will be in 50ths of a second (or 60ths in the US; depending on the network))
frequency) is specified,
n: indicates whether between the individual sections of an effect on
a "Vertical Blank Interrupt" is to be maintained (usually)
not necessary), this usually slows down the execution time (see also
"M", but by which a possible Flashing of the effect area prevented
shall be:
o: indicates how long to wait after performing the effect,
for example, to display the image for ten seconds (will be displayed in "m")
50th or 60th seconds. The specified time period
also includes the possible loading of the next image.

All images must be in IFF-ILBM format. The following screen modes are supported:

Mode | Color Resolution | Color Number
Lores (interlaced) | normal | 2-32
| Extra Halfbrite | 32 Colors + 32 Halftones
| | The first 32 colors
| | (i.e. 64)
| HAM6 | 4096
Hires (interlaced) | normal | 2-16

ATTENTION: when displaying HAM images, you should avoid creating effects. in which vertical lines between background and image/color otherwise the streaks typical for the HAM mode occur.

ATTENTION: the ILBM images must of course be in the current directory lie. The easiest way to achieve this is to place the script file in the Copied directory in which the images are located. Now you start from the workbench, the current directory is already set. Confusion - To avoid, only the script file should receive an icon.

There are currently 20 effects. However, this number increases dramatically, since the parameters "h", "i" and "j" are entered arbitrarily for (almost) every effect can be provided.

Now follows a list of available effects with their required para- metres:

Effect 1 : builds an area in equal blocks from top to top
below (lousie procedure).
Parameter: h: indicates the height of a block.


Effect 2 : builds up an area in bars from left to right.
Parameter: h: indicates the width of a block.


Effect 3 : builds up an area box-shaped (mixing effect 1)
and effect 2.
Parameters: h: indicates how wide and high are copied into each box
(generally, "h" should be equal to the greater of "i") and
"j" so that no empty spaces are created,
i: indicates the width of a box,
j: indicates the height of a box.


Effect 4 : builds up an area in bars from top to bottom.
Parameter: h: indicates the height of a block.


Effect 5 : builds an area in the chessboard pattern from top to bottom,
Then vice versa.
parameter: i: indicates the width of a box,
j: indicates the height of a box.


Effect 6 : builds an area first in blocks from left to right
Each block is omitted. Then, from
to the left, with the missing blocks
are filled.
Parameter: h: indicates the width of a block.


Effect 7 : like effect 6, but from top to bottom, then vice versa.
Parameter: h: indicates the height of a block.


Effect 8 : Builds an area from the center to the corners.
Parameter: i: specifies how many pixels in the x-direction
to be built,
j: specifies how many pixels in the y-direction are simultaneously
is the height of the effect region 100,
while the width is 200, "i" should be set to 2 and "j" to
1 so that they are set up exactly to the corners
becomes


Effect 9 : builds up an area cruciform.
Parameter: i: specifies how many pixels in the x-direction
to be built,
j: specifies how many pixels in the y-direction are simultaneously
should be built (see also note in effect 8).


Effect 10: builds an area tooth-shaped from top to bottom and around
returns.
Parameter: i: indicates the width of a "tooth",
j: specifies how many pixels in the y-direction are simultaneously
to be built.


Effect 11: like effect 10, but from left to right and vice versa.
Parameter: i: specifies how many pixels in the x-direction
to be built,
j: indicates the height of a “tooth”.


Effect 12: Builds an area in blocks from top and bottom to center
on.
Parameter: h: indicates the height of a block.


Effect 13: builds an area in blocks from the center up and
Below.
Parameter: h: indicates the height of a block.


Effect 14: Builds an area in blocks from left and right to center
on.
Parameter: h: indicates the width of a block.


Effect 15: builds an area in blocks from the center to the left and
on the right.
Parameter: h: indicates the width of a block.


Effect 16: builds up an area "circular" (and symmetrical):
-------+
<----+

ShowSlides is used to create script files. After the successful Start opens the editing window, with which existing script files You can change or create new ones. On the surface there is a number of gadgets, a menu is also available.

Creating an effect is very simple:

  • First you set all the parameters,
  • depending on "k" you now search the image file,
  • now you move an effect forward and create a new one.

The gadgets under "Effect", "Screens" and "Different" correspond the parameters mentioned under "Buildup of the script file". The associated Simplifying letters can be used as keyboard abbreviations.

The gadget »image« (shortcut <#>) serves to specify the image file (see also) Menu item »Select image ..« and »Build the script file«.

Search drives

from Gregor Goldbach

Programme description and status

Search drives demonstrates the use of the routines LockDosList(), FindDosEntry() and UnlockDosList() of dos.library from OS 2.04. There shall be: the four possible drives searched in the doslist, the program gives the Result for each drive.

ParsePattern is public domain, do what you want with it. It shall: there is no guarantee that the information is correct or are complete, nor that the program is error-free. Use on their own danger.

Description of the routines LockDosList(), FindDosEntry() and UnlockDosList()

LockDosList() blocks the doslist for other programs, they can then no longer change until UnlockDosList() is called. parameter is the type of information to be present in the doslist, LDF ALL (see modules dos/dosextens) includes among others 'assigns' and 'volumes'; LDF READ stands for reading. As a result, a pointer to the desired Doslist.

FindDosEntry() searches for the Enter the name whose pointer is specified as parameter 2. As third argument must be passed the flags that are already at LockDosList() were used! In the case of running gear, no colon on The end of the name is given. Result is 0 if no entry of this Name could be found, otherwise the routine gives one of 0 different value back.

UnlockDosList() releases the doslist again for other programs. As The only argument is not the pointer on the doslist, but the Pass the flags specified for LockDosList().

imgplugin/-- background--

The image plugin was created because I was looking for a method to create images in Involve EasyGUI projects. Shortly after the appearance of the image- Plugin`s in the AmiNET came some "Clones" in the AmiNET... These clones have some nice "additional functions", e.g. text- output or bevelboxing ect... but the behavior of the image Clicking ect.. does not comply with the guidelines for gadgets that Buttons (Images) remain clicked as long as the mouse button Press remains, whether the pointer is above the image or not. This is solved in the ImgPlugin as in the gadgets and corresponds the directives.

Version 2.0 (Moved to Intuition-Compliant Gadgets!)

newmem/-- Background--

I have programmed the NewMem class (E-Module), since I have already some program crashes due to incorrect memory allocation and/or incorrect memory release, partially caused Sought by my own programs and partly by others "Foreign" programs. In my own programs, I had the opportunity to where the error occurs to search and correct the Others, unfortunately, are not... Now I have the idea to write a class that Simply enables storage allocation and release to over- guard and even fix gross errors (double released) Memory or only partially released memory ect... Surely this is not (yet) a full memory protection, but this class helps (especially programmers) quickly Finding and fixing memory leaks, moreover, it is possible to integrate the module into the final program and thus avoid propagation time errors in memory allocation and catch. But all this should not mean for the programmer that not releasing its requested memory. needs (because that makes the class at the end of the program!), but All this should only help to detect and eliminate errors!

  • At least v37 (Kickstart 2.04) of the Amiga operating system.
  • At least 512Kb of free RAM, 1Mb+ for larger projects
  • edit/compile.
  • At least gadtools.library v37.
  • At least reqtools.library v38.693.
  • AmigaDOS commands TYPE and COPY, in the path or resident.
  • Logical device T: (preferably in RAM:).

EE Completion files

The CompletionFiles file exists in the PROGDIR:prefs path. This file consists of strings which are terminated by a line feed. It was created with EE and can be modified with EE. It shall contain: the path and the name of each file that is blocked by the Complete Block function to be searched.

The predefined CompletionFiles file refers to the files

PROGDIR:prefs/completions/E-Builtin-NoRtnVal and
PROGDIR:prefs/completions/E-builtin.

The predefined files for completion exist as the predefined CompletionFiles file comprising strings which are separated by a line feed are terminated. The text of such a file can all included (as long as they are printable ASCII marks). The allowed Maximum length of the file is in principle unlimited (i.e. only limited) through AmigaDOS and how long you want to wait in a search. The file content is not kept in memory during runtime, Leave it on disc.

If you already have the Complete Block function description If you have read, then you will know that this function is completion file(s). after the first appearance of the marked text searched and, found, the marked block was replaced by the entire row,in which he was found. The specified files can be edited or exchanged with their own. But you must know that the search case-sensitive and that enough text must be marked in order to to obtain unique string, otherwise could You are confused If EE insists the selection by an unexpected Replace the string.

To explain the use of this function: EE uses the function Fgets() of the dos.library to read the lines, and the E function InStr() to make the comparisons.

With some thought, you can easily clearly and Create flexible entries. As an example, the above specified files the patterns of the built-in E Functions. The first file contains the one without results, the latter those with results. Functions with similar names are internal to ordered shortly after long (i.e., Dispose() before DisposeLink(), String()) before StringF()). Now, if I mark the word "OpenS," it's because the structure of the list of completion files is replaced by:

OpenS(width, height, depth, sflags, title, taglist)

but if I mark the word "=OpenS", it will be replaced by:

sptr:=OpenS(width, height, depth, sflags, title, taglist)

Another idea is to give some lines of the source "names". For For example, an entry of a file could include the EasyRequestArgs() line of the EReq.e sample program with a comment at its end:

EasyRequestArgs(0,[20,0,0,body,gadgets],0,args) ->EZREQ

Now when "EZREQ" is completed, the source appears at its Place, and the addition is merely a comment.

EE PrefsEditor: General

The PrefsEditor program is in the directory PROGDIR:bin.

The PrefsEditor command template is 'FILE,PUBSCREEN', with FILE the Optional name of a preset file to be edited and PUBSCREEN is the optional name of a public screen to be 'visited'.

If FILE is not specified, the preset settings used. In this case, the file is stored in T:EE.prefs if the 'Save' button is used to leave the program. One Requester appears, which refers to the creation of this temporary file indicates. It is up to you to manually move the file to a safe location. copying.

If PUBSCREEN is not specified, the workbench is used.

There are three ways to leave the program:

  • Choose 'Cancel' or the Close Window Gadget to change
  • discard and terminate the program.
  • Select 'Save' to make the changes in the command line
  • specified file to save (or T:EE.prefs if no file)
  • was indicated.
  • Select 'Use' if this editor was called from EE and the
  • new settings should only be used in the current session.
  • The settings are stored in T:EE.prefs, the information in the
  • Command line is ignored.

NOTE: PrefsEditor is a standalone utility, so you can Call from the CLI. It can be started by the CLI (or other program starters). Utilities) without a currently running instance of EE to influence.

NOTE: When the PrefsEditor is called from EE and with the 'Use' button left, the settings of the current session can be changed by calling PrefsEditor again in this way. The Changes are stored again in the temporary file. If you Afterwards you should decide to make the temporary changes to keep, you have to T:EE.prefs by hand to a corresponding Copy the place. Do not confuse this with the normal Procedure... this depends only on whether you choose 'use' if you In fact, I mean Save.
