About ...

Code is a program that interrupts the boot process and then after a Codeword asks. This code word is needed to boot the system! The Program is not cancelable, so you can not get through without code. The Program must be entered in the startup sequence before the command >LoadWB<, Or in the user startup. Good is a position at the very beginning of Startup sequence, because you can not interrupt the boot process here.

1. Introduction

This workshop is intended to promote the use of the new module concept under Amiga E from version EC3.0.

In addition to general information, a practicable the creation of their own modules, whose Optimization and its use in own programs demonstrated.

At the same time, some information about the return- of several information from PROCs as well as the Practical use of Amiga data structures.

The workshop modules and all programs addressed herein are Also present on the disk.

Well, what else can I say? Simple: let's go...

2. Modules, what?

With the delivered Amiga E-Packet you have a lot of so-called .m-Files, only what are they?

In these so-called modules, in the older version of the Amiga E compilers (EC2.1, EC2.1b) Information about libraries and data structures.

Definitions of the data structures of the Amiga system are for the Programming of routines that use system functions, eminent important. Without these structures, everyone is forced to work for systems. calls to define needed data structures and values themselves.

But that means a lot of effort and who can already Remember about 5000 data structures and structural values in your head?

The data are to be distinguished in library information, data- Structures and constants.

2.1 Modules for Library Information

An example of the module “mathffp.m” from the “Modules folder” (Note: all modules were equipped with the program "Showmodule") which of the programs delivered to the compiler belongs to:

ShowModule v1.7(c) 1992 $#%!
now showing: "mathffp.m"
NOTE: don't use this output in your code, use the module instead.

LIBRARY mathbase /* informal notation */
SpFix(D0)
SpFlt(D0)
SpCmp(D1,D0)
[..]

SpCeil(D0)
ENDLIBRARY

That looks pretty interesting, right?

For those who do not belong to the System programming is privy, actually very little. And that's what it's supposed to be.

The example should only make clear that in the modules for Library's information is available that is ALL known without modules should have been. And who would like all this, please nice, type, only to use the MathFFP routines?

And so we are already at the first effect of the modules: they Save time!

One and the same module can be used in different programs It is not and must not be entered anew each time.

How such a module is used in its own program, More later.

2.2 Data structures, constants

In addition to libraries, data structures play a major role in Amiga system. It can also be said that the data structures play THE role.

Constants describe values found in the data structures or in system calls may be used. Usually they are Constants nothing more than numerical values, but who already knows himself Does everyone notice? Therefore, each constant has been given a name by which this can be addressed.

And here we have again the same poblem: either all Typing information or .... well, you know, modules- turn.

Modules with data structures look as follows (example: gfx.m from) "Modules/graphics":

ShowModule v1.7(c) 1992 $#%!
now showing: "gfx.m"
NOTE: don't use this output in your code, use the module instead.

CONST BITSET=$8000,
BITCLR=0,
AGNUS=1,
DENISE = 1

(----) OBJECT bitmap
( 0) bytesperrow:INT
( 2) rows:INT
( 4) flags:CHAR
( 5) depth:CHAR
( 6) pad:INT
( 8) planes:substructure
(---) ENDOBJECT /* SIZEOF=40 */

[..]

On the one hand, we see a key word from E: CONST at the beginning. I.e. nothing other than that all subsequent entries constants are.

On the other hand, we see a data structure that also corresponds to the known E-key word "OBJECT" is introduced.

And what can we conclude from all this? We all have these Data helps to save time. A hell of a lot of time for Type in ...

2.3 Modules under EC3.0

With the older EC versions it was quite cumbersome to own Define modules. There was no function in the compiler and so you had to if you needed your own data structures as modules production through support programmes.

In addition, it was also not possible with the old versions, own Programs, PROCS or data definition as modules.

But that has now changed...

Since the version EC3.0 and following, not only Library information, data structures and constants but also procs, own data definitions, etc.

And that's the point. For this we will now enter into the Full boarding ...

3.0 Our first, own module - What should it be able to do?

Let’s start by outlining what our workshop module Let's do it.

Among the E-system functions is a name "KickVersion". These functions do nothing other than that based on the above- This version number checks whether the corresponding Kickstart Version is available or not.

If this exists, TRUE is returned, otherwise false.

The problem with this function, however, is that the actual Kickstart version is returned. And this can be problematic. be ...

For example, you want to write a program that both for Kick 1.3, Kick 2.04 and Kick3.0 have different routines. In this case: In case you have to call this function MORE times to check, Which version actually exists?

How about a function that makes this possible? Light?

In addition, I miss a function that also contains information about displays the CPU or FPU used.

Well, so there we have our functions of the WorkShop module together:

  • a) information about the CPU used,
  • b information about the FPU used,
  • c) Information about the Kickstart version used.

As a minor peculiarity, it should not have 3 different functions give, but only a single function, the three return values returns.

And to give the whole thing another name, let's call the module "SystemInfo"

As I said, this is a workshop on how to use modules. Surely you could also use other modules for div. Problems arising from throw, but that's what you should be able to do after this...

3.1 What do we need?

Well, let's start with point a.

Where do we get the information about the CPU used?

In the Exec library there is a constant that is ATTNFlag called. And right here it says what is used for a CPU in the Amiga will. Since this is a flag, the for- mations in BIT's, i.e. we have to check whether the the corresponding bit for the corresponding CPU is ON or OFF.

The individual flags in detail:

AFF 68040 ---> Amiga has 68040 CPU.
AFF 68030 ---> Amiga has 68030 CPU.
AFF 68020 ---> Amiga has 68020 CPU.
AFF 68010 ---> Amiga has 68010 CPU.

If none of these flags are set, then it is a 60000 CPU.

In addition, however, one can also recognize from the ATTNFlag, which FPU is available:

AFF 68881 ---> Amiga has 68881 FPU.
AFF 68882 ---> Amiga has 68882 FPU.
AFF FPU40 ---> Amiga has 68040 internal FPU.

If none of these flags is set, then no FPU is present.

We would have already done point b. How do we get information about the kick- Start version?

For this, one must know that every library in the Amiga system has a so-called "English Library". has version number. Not exactly with this version number from the Exec library can be found out which kick version of the Amiga used.

3.2 Let's go...

With the tools from the aforementioned chapter we can now ran and write a PROC for this problem:

/***************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************
Syseminfo:Description. A module containing the CPU/FPU -
Types determined and
The kick version. Author: Jörg Wach
(=JCL POWER) :EC version. EC3.0e :OS. > 1.2 :PRG version.
1.0 -> Because it had to be
Without a Kick version
1.1 -> With Kickversion
************************************************************************************ /

OPT MODULE OPT EXPORT

MODULE 'exec/execbase' MODULE 'exec/libraries'

PROC systeminfo()

DEF execBase : PTR TO execbase, attnFlag, cpu, fpu, kick
libbase : PTR TO lib

execBase := execbase
attnFlag := execBase.attnflags

What CPU do we have here? *//

IF (attnFlag AND AFF 68040)
cpu : = 68040
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68030)
cpu : = 68030
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68020)
cpu : = 68020
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68010)
cpu : = 68010
ELSE
cpu : = 68000
ENDIF

/* And is an FPU on board? *//

IF (attnFlag AND AFF 68881)
fpu : = 68881
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF 68882)
fpu = 68882
ELSEIF (attnFlag AND AFF FPU40)
fpu = 68040
ELSE
fpu : = 0
ENDIF

/* And kick version? *//

libbase := execBase.lib
kick := libbase.version

ENDPROC kick, cpu, fpu

Let's take the source code apart, where I block or block. The following lines are used:

1 The Commentary

As a programmer, you should never read the documentation that Forget the version number of a program, etc. That's why I've defined a standard block for myself. which contains some brief information about the source code.

OPT MODULE

This is a new keyword under EC 3.0 and says nothing else than the now following source code a module is. So the compiler also knows that it is from the source code not an executable program.

This keyword must UNCONDITIONALLY first of all for own modules stand.

OPT EXPORT

This is a special keyword for modules only. It shall be WHAT is known from the module other programs may be given.

In other words, this can be controlled by WHICH PROC's, Definitions etc. another program than from this You can know the module.

If this keyword is not used anywhere in the source text, then It means that all functions, constants, etc. are PRIVAT, Other programs may not be announced.

If this keyword is called second in the source code then all subsequent information will be pro- grams made known.

If only individual functions are known to other programs If it wants to do so, then it must do so before the respective functions. Keyword EXPORT is written.

Example:

PROC eins()

ENDPROC

EXPORT PROC two()

[..]

ENDPROC

This means nothing other than that the procedure one() other programs are not announced while the Procedure two other programs is made very well known.

You will certainly ask yourself: what is the point?

This is very easy to answer: if you have a main procedure have which invokes many underprocedures, with other programs communicate only through the main procedure, then it is un- sense, other programs the underprocedures also still known To do it, right?

The PROC to ENDPROC

Needless to say, since we know everything, I have clarified this in the previous chapters.

ENDPROC kick, cpu, fpu

As I said in the definition of objectives, all Values are output from this procedure.

And for this we resort to the special feature of EC3.0: the Return of multiple values.

Well, and so easily you can return several values ....

Yes, and that was all for the source code.

4. Generate a module with EC

I do not need to say much about this, as it is done quite normally. The only exception is that after the lines

Amiga E compiler/assembler/linker v3.0e registered (c) 91/92/93/94 $#%!
lexical analysis ... parsing and compiling ... no errors ... - - - - - - -

no "SystemInfo" file is generated, but a file with the name "SystemInfo.m", because we created a module.

5. Test of the module

Now that we have a module, we want it in See action.

For this we create a small test program that the module and the the PROC systeminfo() contained therein. The issue should be, quite banal, in the CLI.

And here's the test program:

MODULE '*SystemInfo'


PROC main() DEF t1, t2, t3
t1,t2,t3 := systeminfo()
WriteF('\d \d \d',t1, t2, t3)

ENDPROC

Example: CALLREQ PUBLICSCREEN="Workbench"

What is Tab-Expanding?

A special ability that I have in many Unix tools like XEmacs especially appreciate is the ability, after pressure on the Tab key to complete the file name.

That would actually be the whole secret.

FinalExecute does the same.

How do I use this ability?

If you enter the beginning or fragment of a name, try (the program) to divide the fragment into path and file part. Date A path is present in this after the name pattern, the file sought. If it does not exist, it tries to the current directory to find the pattern is also not possible, it searches the device, assign or drive list, If it is not found, he does nothing. But he finds one. Conformity, so he sets them in, he finds several he opens Window in which you then find the appropriate file or the appropriate can select a directory. If the cursor is on a blank or at the beginning of a name, he opens a file quester in which Then you can pick out the name(s) you were looking for.

You can use DOS patterns if you want.

So as you can see, a blessing for people who prefer anyway Use a finger to enter commands! :

The EPD is dead or long live the EPD

Hello dear e-church!

Many know me from the many letters I sent to e-enthusiastic users I have written. Some know me from the registrations that I have have been made.

And I also want to come straight to the point: I will be for longer Make period NOTHING more for the EPD series!

"Why this" will now raise some questions. Then let's leave it short. Take a little history...

It was on 1 July 1993. On this historical date, the number 1 of the EPD series the light of the world. Unfortunately, the post also provided the ZIP codes, but this was just an action "under further ran" ;

The announcement and release of the disk at that time prompted many to Such statements as "again a new series!" There are already such many ..." or other, highly motivating statements.

But since I did not let it scare me, I still appeared in the same Year number 2 and 3.

Well, and then it began that the programming language E was no longer a It was a programming language, but it became a serious language. Language has developed in the Amiga sector.

It followed the year 1994, in which the series achieved a rapid rise was able to record. Say and write another 13 disks saw the light of day.

And then followed the record year 1995: until 1.7.1995 again appeared Another 14 disks. And they weren't all programs yet. They were in the E-pool.

The fact is: the series could not bring out as many disks as There were programs.

The main problem was me: my time. It is, as many know, It was extremely narrow and limited.

And now the time has been reached when I received the letters in many "If my time permits it!" to the bitter The truth must be told.

My time does not allow the series anymore! I can, especially wg. my studies, for one year (roundabout until 1.7.1996) definitely nothing Do more for the series!

And so the question arises: what happens to the EPD now?

Well, let's look at the alternatives:

1. setting the series

This is a possibility I have considered.

But this would also have meant for many that a corresponding software pool, as it is the EPD, no longer exists. And so the language would have become uninteresting to many what I (and Wouter, too, would be very sorry.

That is why this solution is the worst there can be.

Compulsory break until next year

Another possibility, but for many also a bad one Solution. Because in the meantime, according to my projections, there would be material for Another 30 disks came out.

And no one knew about it...

Continuation by someone new

As you can read on any EPD, the floppy disk series is Daniel van Gerpen created and distributed.

Daniel, after short pleas and threats (hi Daniel :) She agrees to continue the series.

Furthermore, another e-programmer will be in the Preparation of the EPD: Gregor Goldbach. Also for many due to An acquaintance of his AEE project.

Yes, and that is why we can continue to live the EPD!

Many will have to get used to the two new contacts, but Do not worry, the "you" is also familiar to the two :

Let's move on to a few detailed questions that are still open:

- What happens to the subscriptions I have?

No problem. Take the two on the same terms as I closed it with you.

Please register new subscriptions directly with Daniel or Gregor.

- Now what happens to the projects that some started with me have they?

Well, let's list them in detail:

  • E-NETZ: I will continue to push. Please do not expect
  • Miracles. You cannot hurry to rebuild something that
  • It was only broken.
  • Game mods: will also continue to run, as Danny (Hi)
  • Danny :) wants to support very strongly.
  • Registrations: I will continue as these
  • are time-uncritical.
  • The book on E: will be published this year if possible.

And now we want to announce the addresses, so that everyone knows where to get the new EPDs:

Daniel van Gerpen Gregor Goldbach
Old Postal Route 3 Green Route 10

26759 Rear 21423 Pattensen

EMAIL: agnus@… glauschwuffel@…

Well, I just wish everyone a lot of fun with the two of them. Good luck to both of them...

Jörg in August 1995

P.S.: Don't forget: the WoC in Cologne.

On 11.11.95 I will be like the Creme de la Creme of the e-programmers And maybe Wouter is there.

When: 11.11.95, 13.00 at the stand of APLUS or ICP (if APLUS does not have its own stand.

source package on Aminet ↗

append() - Copyright © 2-Jul-1995 by Maik "BLiZZeR" Schreiber

append() does nothing other than Open() - it opens a file and gives return the address of the filehandle. However, append() serves for attaching data to a file.

If the file could be opened because it already existed, the "Write cursor" positioned so that you are at the end of the file. If the file did not already exist, it will be reopened.

Call for proposals

An example of the call:

IF handle:=append(filename)
.
.

Close(handle)
ENDIF
handle - the normal file handle as in Open()
filename - the filename as in Open()

  • Library functions

  • Overview: How are you?

The cdplayer.library is a library for controlling SCSI-CD-Rom- running gear. It allows convenient control of the audio functions, when an audio CD is in the drive.

My biggest thanks go to Gary Duncan from whose SCSIUtil I most I learned things for this library. In addition, my thanks go to Thomas Herold, who helped me overcome initial difficulties The old cdplayer.library helped.

This library and the included files are all FreeWare that Copyright remains with me, the use is cost-free. This library may are freely copied and stored in mailboxes/mailbox networks/Internet and as long as no profit is made on this package.

The use of this library in own programs is of course permitted, but with (small) conditions. These hang out with the Type of distribution/form of software together:

Holsteinstr. 27 27
41564 Kaarst

/include/libraries/cdplay.h:

The cdplay.library is based on the CDRequest. A CDRom as To use audio players, the function CDOpenDriver() is used. As parameter it gets the SCSI device of the drive and the ID of the CD-Rom's. A pointer is then delivered to a structure of the type CDRequest. This structure requires EVERY function of the library. After In use, the structure is deleted again with CDCloseDrive(), memory released and the device closed. After opening must be self-contained Check whether it is also an audio CD.

The "struct CDRequest" contains the following entries, structures are further described in more detail below:

struct IOStdReq *cdr Request;

An IOStdReq for communication of the library with device. Intact In principle, this structure is private, who can use it for their own purposes You want to use it at your own risk.

struct MsgPort *cdr MsgPort;

A message port for device communication.

struct CDCapacity *cdr Capacity;

This structure provides information about some parameters of the CD, e.g. Size/Length etc.

struct CDInquiry *cdr Inquiry;

Information about the device.

struct CDPTOC *cdr TOC;

The table of contents of the CD.

struct CDTime *cdr Time;

Information about the current track times, total playing time of the CD and similar information.

struct CDVolume *cdr Volume;

Volume of the CD-Rom, currently unused.

UBYTE cdr ID[20];

Each CD gets an ID, which (hopefully ;) only occurs once. As a result, the CD can be identified again at any time. This ID is compatible with those using MCDP or BGUIPlayer.

UBYTE cdr Active;

Outputs the current state of the drive, are possible

SCSI STAT NO DISK no CD in the drive
SCSI STAT PLAYING an audio CD is played
SCSI STAT STOPPED CD in drive, is not played
SCSI STAT PAUSED pause function is active
UBYTE cdr CurrentTrack;

The current track that is currently being played. This value is only valid if cdr Active on SCSI STAT PLAYING or ... PAUSED In all other cases, the result is undefined.

ULONG cdr CurrentAddress;

Current addresses on the CD, this value can be used e.g. with the Macros base2min() and base2sec() are converted into a real time.

UBYTE *cdr SCSISense;
UBYTE *cdr SCSIData
UBYTE *cdr TOCBuf

3 internal buffers, FINGER WAY! Manipulations on these buffers It can have very strange consequences...

The "struct CDCapacity" gives 3 information about the inserted CD:

ULONG cdc MaxSector;

Number of sectors of the CD.

ULONG cdc SectorSize;

Size of a sector (usually this should be 2048 bytes)

ULONG cdc Capacity;

The capacity of the CD (cdr MaxSector * cdr Capacity)

The "struct CDInquiry" provides information about the CD-Rom used:

ULONG cdi Flags;

The possible flags are defined in libraries/cdplay.h, a An explanation is not necessary to be able to use the library fully. If someone is interested in the info, he will be named in the Include can start enough.

UBYTE cdi DeviceType;
DEVTYPE DIRECT ACCESS hard drives etc.
DEVTYPE SEQUENTIAL ACCESS Streamer etc.
DEVTYPE PRINTER printer
DEVTYPE PROCESSOR processor devices
DEVTYPE WRITE ONCE WORM drives
DEVTYPE CDROM CDRom if a device is equipped with
using cdplay.library
Should it be, must be on this
Flag tested.
DEVTYPE SCANNER scanner
DEVTYPE OPTICAL Optical Media
DEVTYPE MEDIUM CHANGER Jukeboxen, Changer, ...
DEVTYPE COMMUNICATIONS Communication devices
DEVTYPE ASC IT8 1 \
DEVTYPE ASC IT8 2 > explains itself
DEVTYPE UNKNOWN
UBYTE cdi ANSIVersion;

The ANSI version of the device, here the following values are possible:

ANSI NONE not standardized
ANSI SCSI 1 SCSI-I Device
ANSI SCSI 2 SCSI-II Device
[ ... ]
UBYTE cdi VendorID[9];

Manufacturer name as ASCII, 0 terminated.

UBYTE cdi ProductID[17];

Product name, 0 terminated.

UBYTE cdi RevisionLevel[5];

Version of the firmware, again 0 terminated.

UBYTE cdi VendorSpecific[21];

Manufacturer-specific text/data.

UBYTE cdi Reserved[36];

Reserved part.

The "struct CDPTOC" is the table of contents of a CD. It shall consist of: the following data:

ULONG cdptoc TOCSize;

Internal value

UBYTE cdptoc FirstTrack;

First track on the CD.

UBYTE cdptoc LastTrack;

Last track on the CD.

struct CDTrack cdptoc Track[100];

Array with information about the tracks. On a CD can not More than 100 tracks. For each CD cdtoc LastTrack - cdtoc FirstTrack Tracks and thus also Trackinfos ready.

The "struct CDTrack" contains data for each track on the CD, also for Data area, which is usually the first track:

ULONG tr Position;

Start position on the CD, this address can be used with the Macros base2min() and base2sec() can be converted in minutes and seconds and is the start time.

ULONG tr Flags;

Flags that describe the track, e.g.

IFLAG COPY PROHIBITED Track may not be copied
IFLAG AUDIO TRACK Audiotrack
UBYTE tr SubChan;

SubChan information.

The "struct CDTime" is included in the CDRequest and is replaced by CDUpdate() filled with up-to-date information about playtime. All values can with the base2min() and base2sec() Macros into real values.

The first 3 values refer to the current track, the last 3 to The complete CD:

ULONG cdt TrackCurBase;

Current time

ULONG cdt TrackRemainBase;

Time remaining

ULONG cdt TrackCompleteBase;

Total playing time

ULONG cdt AllCurBase;

Current time

ULONG cdt AllRemainBase;

Time remaining

ULONG cdt AllCompleteBase;

Total playing time

The two Macros

#define base2min(val) ((val)/75/60)
#define base2sec(val) ((val)/75)%60)

serve for the position on the CD of an address in time values conversion. For example, I just got the current status of the CD, This is a line like this.

printf ("%02d:%02d", base2min (my cdrequest->cdr CurrentAddress),
base2sec (my cdrequest->cdr CurrentAddress));

For example, "12:44".

To test bits more easily I use i.d.rule in my sources Macros, which I also make available to the users of my library Wishes:

test a bit: #define btst(n,m)(n & m)
convert one bit: #define bchg(n,m) (n = (n & m) ? (n & (~m)) : (n | m))
test one bit: #define bset(n,m) (n = n | m)

Here is a short overview: what to do to create a CD with the library Playable:

  • Set CDOpenDriver() on a SCSI drive
  • check in the returned structure whether the device also
  • It really is a CDRom.
  • is the track I want to play also an audio track?
  • Do not forget CDCloseDrive() at the end!

checkbin() - Copyright © 2-Jul-1995 by Maik "BLiZZeR" Schreiber

checkbin() is a simple binary check for files. It reads the desired Number of bytes from a file that are then checked.

The following ASCII characters are considered to be indicators of binaries: 0-8, 11-12, 14-26, 28-31 and 128-159.

Call for proposals

am:=checkbin(filename,checklength)
bin - TRUE if the file is binary, FALSE if not
filename - path to the file to be checked (e.g. "RAM:Test.dat")
checklength - number of characters checked from the beginning of the file
They may be more than the length of the file.

zconmsg() - Copright © 1-Jul-1995 by Maik Schreiber

source package on Aminet ↗

zconmsg() - Copright © 1-Jul-1995 by Maik Schreiber

With zconmsg() it is possible in AmigaE programs to create a ZConnect-compliant Attach mail to a buffer file. With zconmsg(), both text and binaries are also used, zconmsg() recognizes this automatically.

The call of zconmsg() is as follows:

Syntax : zconmsg(buffer,mail,emp,bet,abs,eda,mid)
Example : zconmsg('RAM:Test buffer.txt', 'RAM:Test.txt'),
'BLiZZeR@…','Testmail','HeinBloed',
'19950701010314S+2','12345@heinbloed'
Parameters: buffer =path of the output buffer
mail = path to the mail file used as mail content
shall:
emp = receiver \
bet = subject \
abs = sender } must have all ZConnect format
eda = date of creation /
mid = Message ID /

zconmsg() now attaches the mail file mail to the output buffer puffer in the form of A ZConnect mail.

Author
